sectionsPreview.summary: Defines the eight lawful recipients of Zakah and contrasts the mutual support of believers with the corruption of hypocrites.

sectionsPreview.summary: Condemns hypocrites who broke their vows of charity, mocked poor donors, and rejoiced at staying behind from Tabuk.

sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts hypocritical Bedouins with sincere ones and praises the foremost Muhajirin, Ansar, and those who follow them in virtue.

sectionsPreview.summary: Accepts the repentance of believers who confessed staying behind, commands taking purifying alms, and orders demolishing the Mosque of Harm.

sectionsPreview.title: Allah's Purchase of Believers' Lives, Ibrahim's Prayer & the Three Companions

sectionsPreview.summary: Records every hardship in Jihad, mandates that a group study religion deeply, and extols the Prophet's profound compassion.

sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts those content merely with worldly life who face the Fire with believers guided to rivers and peace in Paradise.

sectionsPreview.summary: Challenges doubters to produce a single surah, affirms that people wrong only themselves, and depicts the terror of Resurrection.

sectionsPreview.summary: Presents the Qur'an as a cure for hearts and rebukes those who arbitrarily declare Allah's lawful provisions unlawful.

sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms Allah's knowledge of every atom, guarantees peace for His friends (Awliya'), and recounts Nuh and Musa confronting tyranny.

sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs Bani Isra'il to establish prayer in their Egyptian homes and records Allah accepting Musa and Harun's supplication.

sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Pharaoh's futile declaration of faith while drowning and the preservation of his body as a lasting sign.

sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights how sincere repentance saved Yunus's people from impending doom and commands unwavering devotion to Allah alone.

sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the destruction of Thamud by the terrible Cry after slaughtering the she-camel and the angels visiting Ibrahim.

sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the angels giving Sarah glad tidings of Ishaq and Ya'qub, Ibrahim's pleading, and Lut's distress over his people.

sectionsPreview.summary: Details the destruction of Sodom by stones of baked clay and Shu'aib's command to Madyan for honest measures.

sectionsPreview.summary: Chronicles the ruin of Madyan, Pharaoh leading his people into the Fire, and the contrasting fates of the wretched and blessed.

sectionsPreview.summary: Commands unwavering uprightness on the straight path, forbids inclining toward tyrants, and shows how prayers erase minor sins.

sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that Allah never destroys just societies, strengthens the Prophet's heart through prophetic narratives, and enjoins trust in Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: The 'Best of Stories' detailing Prophet Yusuf's patience through betrayal, servitude, false imprisonment, and ultimate royal elevation in Egypt.

sectionsPreview.summary: Presents Yusuf's eloquent discourse on monotheism in prison, his interpretation of his cellmates' dreams, and the king's vision.

sectionsPreview.summary: Details how the sun, moon, stars, seas yielding fresh meat and pearls, and firm mountains serve humanity.

sectionsPreview.summary: Traces Dhul-Qarnain's just expeditions to the setting and rising points of the sun and a mountain pass.

sectionsPreview.title: Barrier Against Gog and Magog and Vain Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Dhul-Qarnain constructing the iron barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj and warns of deeds ruined by disbelief.

sectionsPreview.title: Reward of Firdaus and Pure Monotheistic Worship
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the worthless deeds of disbelievers with eternal Firdaus and concludes with the call to pure monotheism.

surahs.thematicSummary: The miraculous births of Yahya and 'Isa, the chastity of Maryam, and the monotheistic heritage of early prophetic dynasties.

sectionsPreview.title: Secret Supplication of Zakariyya for an Heir
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the aged Prophet Zakariyya's humble, private prayer asking Allah for a righteous successor from His grace.

sectionsPreview.title: Glad Tidings of Yahya and Childhood Wisdom
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates the miraculous birth of Prophet Yahya to barren parents, Zakariyya's three-day silence, and Yahya's early wisdom.

sectionsPreview.title: Virtues of Yahya and Jibra'il's Appearance to Maryam
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises Yahya's compassion and filial piety, then recounts Maryam's seclusion and the angel Jibra'il appearing to her.

sectionsPreview.title: Miraculous Conception and Birth of Prophet 'Isa
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the angelic announcement of a pure son, Maryam's childbirth by the palm trunk, and her silence vow.

sectionsPreview.title: Defense of Maryam and 'Isa's Cradle Speech
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Maryam returning to her accusing people and infant 'Isa miraculously proclaiming his prophethood and servitude.

sectionsPreview.title: True Nature of 'Isa and Christian Excess
sectionsPreview.summary: Completes 'Isa's cradle speech, refutes the claim that Allah took a son, and introduces Prophet Ibrahim.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Tender Counsel and His Blessed Progeny
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents Ibrahim's respectful plea to his idol-worshipping father, his peaceful departure, and his blessed prophetic descendants.

sectionsPreview.title: Commendation of Prophets Musa, Harun, and Isma'il
sectionsPreview.summary: Honors Musa's intimate communion at Mount Tur alongside Harun and praises Isma'il's truthfulness to his promise.

sectionsPreview.title: Devotion of Isma'il and Idris and Weeping Prophets
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights Isma'il enjoining prayer on his family, Idris's high station, and prophets falling in weeping prostration.

sectionsPreview.title: Negligent Successors, Eternal Gardens, and Certain Resurrection
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts prayer-neglecting generations with repentant believers entering Paradise, and affirms that disbelievers will kneel around Hell.

sectionsPreview.title: Crossing Over Hellfire and Everlasting Virtues
sectionsPreview.summary: States that everyone will pass over Hell while the God-fearing are saved, exposing worldly delusion.

sectionsPreview.title: Arrogant Boasts and Betrayal by False Deities
sectionsPreview.summary: Refutes the boastful disbeliever claiming future wealth in the Hereafter and warns that idols will disown worshippers.

sectionsPreview.title: Respite for Disbelievers and Gathering the Righteous
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that devils incite disbelievers while their days are numbered, before the righteous are gathered as honored guests.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Indignation at Attributing a Son to Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares the cosmos nearly bursts at attributing a son to Allah, affirming all creation are His servants.

sectionsPreview.title: Silent Ruins of Destroyed Generations Before Them
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes by reminding the disbelievers of countless mighty generations destroyed before them without leaving a single whisper.

surahs.thematicSummary: Consolation of the Prophet, Musa's vision of the burning bush at Mount Tuwa, confrontation with Pharaoh, and the golden calf.

sectionsPreview.title: The Qur'an as a Merciful Divine Reminder
sectionsPreview.summary: Consoles the Prophet that the Qur'an was revealed not as hardship, but as a reminder from the Creator.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Omniscience and Musa's Call at Tuwa
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms Allah's knowledge of deepest secrets and recounts Musa seeing the fire and being chosen in Tuwa.

sectionsPreview.title: Establishing Prayer and Miracle of the Staff
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands Musa to worship Allah alone, establish prayer, prepare for the Hour, and cast down his staff.

sectionsPreview.title: Two Miraculous Signs and Musa's Prayer
sectionsPreview.summary: Displays the serpent staff and radiant hand, commissions Musa to confront Pharaoh, and begins his supplication.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Supplication for Eloquence and Harun's Support
sectionsPreview.summary: Records Musa's prayer for clear speech and for his brother Harun to share his prophetic mission.

sectionsPreview.title: Acceptance of Musa's Prayer and Childhood Favors
sectionsPreview.summary: Assures Musa that his request is granted and reminds him of divine protection during infancy and Madyan.

sectionsPreview.title: Speaking Gently to Pharaoh and Dialogue on Lordship
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs Musa and Harun to address Pharaoh gently and recounts their dialogue regarding the Creator and past generations.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Earth and Scheduling Pharaoh's Contest
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights Allah's earthly provisions and narrates Pharaoh accusing Musa of sorcery and setting the festival-day contest.

sectionsPreview.title: Pharaoh's Magicians and Their Secret Counsel
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Pharaoh gathering his sorcerers, Musa warning them against fabricating lies, and their debate before the contest.

sectionsPreview.title: Triumph of Musa's Staff and Magicians' Faith
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Musa's staff swallowing the magicians' illusions, their immediate prostration in faith, and defiance of Pharaoh's threats.

sectionsPreview.title: Salvation of Bani Isra'il and Wilderness Favors
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes the magicians' testimony, recounts Pharaoh's drowning, and recalls blessings upon Bani Isra'il before Musa's mountaintop appointment.

sectionsPreview.title: Trial of the Golden Calf and Musa's Return
sectionsPreview.summary: Informs Musa that Samiri misled his people with a lowing golden calf, prompting Musa's sorrowful rebuke.

sectionsPreview.title: Harun's Plea, Samiri's Banishment, and Heavy Burdens
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Harun's defense before Musa, the banishment of Samiri, and the heavy burden of rejecting the Qur'an.

sectionsPreview.title: Terror of Resurrection and Warning to Adam
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the Day of the Trumpet, instructs patience in receiving revelation, and recalls Iblis's enmity toward Adam.

sectionsPreview.title: Adam's Slip, Forgiveness, and Straitened Heedless Life
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Satan's temptation of Adam, Adam's repentance, and the blind resurrection of those who ignore Allah's reminder.

sectionsPreview.title: Patience, Steadfast Prayer, and Worldly Detachment
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands the Prophet to bear insults patiently, celebrate Allah's praise, and disregard the fleeting splendor of disbelievers.

surahs.thematicSummary: The closeness of humanity's reckoning, cosmic unity of creation, Ibrahim's trial by fire, and the sending of the Prophet as mercy to all worlds.

sectionsPreview.title: Approaching Reckoning and Heedless Mockery of Disbelievers
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns that humanity's reckoning is near while people remain heedless, dismissing revelation as dreams, poetry, or sorcery.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Messengers and Destruction of Unjust Towns
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that all previous messengers were mortal men receiving revelation and describes the ruin of mocking communities.

sectionsPreview.title: Purposeful Cosmic Creation and Devotion of Angels
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that the cosmos was not created in jest, truth crushes falsehood, and angels worship tirelessly.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Order as Proof of Divine Unity
sectionsPreview.summary: Proves that multiple deities would have thrown the cosmos into chaos and affirms Allah's unquestioned sovereignty.

sectionsPreview.title: Servitude of Angels and Signs in Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Refutes claims that angels are Allah's daughters and points to cosmic origins, life-giving water, and mountains.

sectionsPreview.title: Celestial Orbits, Universal Mortality, and Sudden Torment
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights the orbits of sun and moon, reminds that every soul tastes death, and warns of sudden punishment.

sectionsPreview.title: Scales of Justice and Ibrahim Smashing Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms the precise weighing of deeds, recalls the Torah, and narrates Ibrahim confronting his people's idols.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Argument, Cool Fire, and Prophetic Line
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Ibrahim silencing the idolaters, Allah making the fire cool for him, and blessing him with righteous prophets.

sectionsPreview.title: Deliverance of Lut and Wisdom of Dawud
sectionsPreview.summary: Mentions the salvation of Lut and Nuh and recounts the judicial wisdom bestowed upon Dawud and Sulaiman.

sectionsPreview.title: Subjugation of Wind and Patience of Ayyub
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Dawud's armor-making, the wind and jinn subjugated to Sulaiman, and Allah answering Ayyub's cry in affliction.

sectionsPreview.title: Patient Prophets and the Cry of Yunus
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises the patience of Isma'il, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, recounts Yunus's supplication in darkness, and introduces Zakariyya's prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Acceptance of Zakariyya, Maryam, and One Brotherhood
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates the blessing of Yahya, honors Maryam and 'Isa, and declares all prophets part of one united faith.

sectionsPreview.title: Gog and Magog and Security of Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, idols becoming fuel for Hell, and believers safe from terror.

sectionsPreview.title: Rolling Up the Sky and Universal Mercy
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the sky rolled up like a scroll, promises earth to the righteous, and proclaims universal prophetic mercy.

surahs.thematicSummary: The earthquake of the Hour, the rites and spiritual objectives of Hajj, sacrificial animals, and permission for defensive struggle.

sectionsPreview.title: Convulsion of the Hour and Resurrection Proofs
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns mankind of the terrifying earthquake of the Hour and cites embryology and plant revival as resurrection proofs.

sectionsPreview.title: Wavering Faith, Cosmic Prostration, and Final Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Exposes opportunistic faith that wavers during trials, affirms all creation prostrates to Allah, and contrasts Hell with Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Rewards of Paradise and the Sacred Mosque
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the adornments of Paradise, warns against blocking Al-Masjid Al-Haram, and recalls Ibrahim purifying the Ka'bah.

sectionsPreview.title: Proclamation of Hajj and Avoidance of Idolatry
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the command to Ibrahim to proclaim the Hajj pilgrimage, details its rites, and condemns polytheism.

sectionsPreview.title: Revering Allah's Symbols and Rites of Sacrifice
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that honoring Allah's symbols stems from heart-felt piety and explains the spiritual purpose of sacrificial rites.

sectionsPreview.title: Spirit of Sacrifice and Permission for Defensive Jihad
sectionsPreview.summary: Clarifies that Taqwa reaches Allah in sacrifice and grants oppressed believers permission to fight in self-defense.

sectionsPreview.title: Philosophy of Defensive Struggle and Ruined Cities
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that defensive war protects houses of worship, outlines righteous governance, and warns against spiritual blindness.

sectionsPreview.title: Protection of Revelation and Reward of Martyrs
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms how Allah nullifies satanic whispers around revelation, honors slain migrants, and highlights signs of divine omnipotence.

sectionsPreview.title: Powerlessness of Idols and Call to Worship
sectionsPreview.summary: Exposes the inability of idols to create a fly and exhorts believers to bow, prostrate, and do good.

sectionsPreview.title: Striving for Allah and Legacy of Ibrahim
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes with the command to strive sincerely for Allah, affirm the ease of Islam, and witness to humanity.

surahs.thematicSummary: The defining characteristics of successful believers in Salah and chastity, human embryology, and the eternal abode of Firdaus.

sectionsPreview.title: Moral and Spiritual Qualities of Successful Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Defines the successful believers by their humble prayer, avoidance of vain talk, Zakah, chastity, and trustworthiness.

sectionsPreview.title: Guarding Prayers, Inheriting Firdaus, and Human Origin
sectionsPreview.summary: Completes the portrait of believers who inherit Firdaus by guarding prayers and begins the account of human creation.

sectionsPreview.title: Embryonic Development Stages and Inevitability of Death
sectionsPreview.summary: Traces human development in the womb from sperm-drop to clot, lump, bones, and flesh, followed by death.

sectionsPreview.title: Resurrection, Seven Heavens, and Measured Rainfall
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms resurrection on Judgment Day and points to the creation of seven heavens and measured water on earth.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Orchards, Olive Trees, and Livestock
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes how rainwater produces date-palm and grape gardens, the blessed olive tree of Sinai, and nourishing cattle.

sectionsPreview.title: Mission of Nuh and Rejection of Resurrection
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Nuh's preaching, the Ark's deliverance from the flood, and the next generation's denial of life after death.

sectionsPreview.title: Succession of Messengers to Musa and 'Isa
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the destruction of nations who denied resurrection and traces the prophetic chain through Musa, Harun, and 'Isa.

sectionsPreview.title: Unity of Prophetic Faith Versus Sectarian Division
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms the single creed of all prophets, rebukes sectarian fragmentation, and contrasts deluded materialists with God-fearing believers.

sectionsPreview.title: Foremost in Good Works and Sinners' Regret
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises believers who hasten to good deeds within their capacity and depicts the futile cries of seized transgressors.

sectionsPreview.title: Arrogant Rejection and Stubborn Persistence in Error
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebukes the Makkans for scorning the Qur'an in night-time tales and refusing to humble themselves despite truth.

sectionsPreview.title: Acknowledgment of the Creator and Divine Unity
sectionsPreview.summary: Uses the polytheists' own admission of Allah's sovereignty over creation to refute their denial of resurrection and polytheism.

sectionsPreview.title: Repelling Evil With Good and Seeking Refuge
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs the Prophet to repel hostility with the best conduct and seek Allah's refuge from satanic promptings.

sectionsPreview.title: Deathbed Regret and the Barrier of Barzakh
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the dying disbeliever's futile plea to return to earth and establishes the Barzakh barrier until Resurrection.

sectionsPreview.title: Severing of Kinship and Weighing of Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the blowing of the Trumpet, the weighing of deeds, and the confession of the damned in Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Rebuke of the Damned and Prayer for Mercy
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes with Allah's rebuke to those who mocked believers, earthly life's brevity, and a prayer for forgiveness.

surahs.thematicSummary: Social decorum, domestic privacy, the Verse of Light (Ayat an-Nur), vindication of Sayyidah 'A'ishah, and modest dress codes.

sectionsPreview.title: Prescribed Punishments for Fornication and False Accusation
sectionsPreview.summary: Ordains the legal punishments for unlawful sexual intercourse and for slandering chaste women without producing four witnesses.

sectionsPreview.title: Procedure of Li'an and the Slander Incident
sectionsPreview.summary: Establishes the mutual oath procedure (Li'an) between spouses and addresses the fabricated slander against Sayyidah 'A'ishah.

sectionsPreview.title: Rebuke for Spreading Rumors and Speech Etiquette
sectionsPreview.summary: Admonishes believers who repeated the slander without proof, warning that casual gossip is grave before Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Condemning Indecency and Forgiveness Toward Fellow Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns those who spread immorality, exhorts Abu Bakr to forgive mistreated kin, and affirms full accountability.

sectionsPreview.title: Purity of the Righteous and Entering Homes
sectionsPreview.summary: Vindicates the pure from slander and legislates seeking permission and offering Salam before entering private residences.

sectionsPreview.title: Lowering the Gaze, Modesty, and Facilitating Marriage
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands believing men and women to guard their gaze and modesty, promote marriage, and protect slave-women.

sectionsPreview.title: Parable of Divine Light and Devout Mosques
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents the luminous parable of Allah's Light in a believer's heart and praises mosques frequented by the pious.

sectionsPreview.title: Mirage of Disbelief, Cosmic Worship, and Hypocrites
sectionsPreview.summary: Likens disbelievers' deeds to a mirage, highlights nature's glorification of Allah, and exposes hypocrites evading prophetic judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Wholehearted Obedience, Khilafah Promise, and Domestic Privacy
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts believers' obedience with hypocrites, promises earthly succession (Khilafah) to the faithful, and sets domestic privacy rules.

sectionsPreview.title: Modesty for Elderly Women and Collective Etiquette
sectionsPreview.summary: Clarifies dress concessions for elderly women, permits shared family meals, and requires seeking leave during collective duties.

surahs.thematicSummary: The Quran as the criterion between truth and falsehood, celestial signs, and the noble virtues of the Servants of the Most Merciful ('Ibad ar-Rahman).

sectionsPreview.title: Revelation of the Criterion and Polytheist Objections
sectionsPreview.summary: Glorifies Allah for revealing the Criterion and refutes polytheist objections regarding the Prophet's humanity and the Qur'an.

sectionsPreview.title: Demands to See Angels and Evil Companions
sectionsPreview.summary: Addresses the disbelievers' demand to see angels or Allah and depicts wrongdoers lamenting corrupt friends on Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Forsaking the Qur'an and Gradual Revelation Wisdom
sectionsPreview.summary: Records the Prophet's complaint against his people forsaking the Qur'an, explains its gradual revelation, and recalls Musa.

sectionsPreview.title: Destroyed Nations, Worship of Desires, and Nature
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalls the fate of Nuh, 'Ad, and Thamud, rebukes worshipping desires, and highlights shadows, sleep, and winds.

sectionsPreview.title: Revival by Rain and Barrier Between Seas
sectionsPreview.summary: Reflects on rainwater reviving dead land, the barrier separating sweet and salty seas, and human creation from water.

sectionsPreview.title: Reliance on Allah and Servants of Ar-Rahman
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands reliance on the Ever-Living Lord, rebukes rejection of Ar-Rahman, and introduces the humble Servants of the All-Merciful.

sectionsPreview.title: Night Vigil, Moderation, and Sincere Repentance
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the Servants of Ar-Rahman through night prayers, balanced spending, avoiding major sins, and sincere repentance.

sectionsPreview.title: Dignified Conduct, Pious Offspring, and Eternal Paradise
sectionsPreview.summary: Completes the portrait of the Servants of Ar-Rahman who shun falsehood, pray for pious families, and attain Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Importance of Supplication and Punishment of Denial
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes by declaring that human worth before Allah rests on supplication, warning deniers of inescapable torment.

surahs.thematicSummary: Rhythmic accounts of prophets meeting obstinate deniers, the true nature of Quranic revelation, and contrast with frivolous poets.

sectionsPreview.title: The Manifest Book and Consoling the Prophet
sectionsPreview.summary: Opens with the clarity of the Qur'an and consoles the Prophet over his grief at the Makkans' disbelief.

sectionsPreview.title: Heedlessness, Signs in Vegetation, and Musa's Commission
sectionsPreview.summary: Notes how disbelievers mock every reminder despite signs in vegetation, and introduces Musa's call to confront Pharaoh.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Dialogue With Pharaoh and Gathering Sorcerers
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Musa and Harun confronting Pharaoh over Bani Isra'il, debating the Lord, and summoning Egypt's magicians.

sectionsPreview.title: Defeat of the Sorcerers and Pharaoh's Threat
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Musa's staff swallowing the magicians' ropes, their immediate declaration of faith, and Pharaoh's threat of crucifixion.

sectionsPreview.title: Steadfastness of the Magicians and Exodus
sectionsPreview.summary: Records the magicians' fearless devotion to Allah and narrates Pharaoh's army pursuing Bani Isra'il out of Egypt.

sectionsPreview.title: Parting the Sea and Ibrahim Against Idolatry
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the miraculous parting of the sea for Musa and transitions to Ibrahim's critique of idols.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Supplication for Remembrance and Forgiveness
sectionsPreview.summary: Continues Ibrahim's prayer for a truthful reputation among later generations, inheritance of Paradise, and protection from disgrace.

sectionsPreview.title: The Sound Heart and Preaching of Nuh
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that only a sound heart benefits on Judgment Day, depicts idolaters' regrets, and introduces Nuh's mission.

sectionsPreview.title: Deliverance of Nuh and Hud's Admonition
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Nuh defending his humble followers before the flood and recounts Hud rebuking the arrogant tribe of 'Ad.

sectionsPreview.title: Destruction of Thamud and Warning of Lut
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes Salih's warning to Thamud and narrates Lut condemning his people's shameless transgression and his family's deliverance.

sectionsPreview.title: Ruin of Lut's People and Shu'aib's Call
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the rain of stones upon Lut's city and introduces Shu'aib preaching monotheism and honest measure.

sectionsPreview.title: Command for Just Weights and Shu'aib's Rejection
sectionsPreview.summary: Records Shu'aib's command to weigh with an even balance and his people's demand for punishment from the sky.

sectionsPreview.title: Day of Canopy and the Trustworthy Spirit
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the destruction of Aikah by the Canopy torment and affirms the Qur'an's descent via Jibra'il.

sectionsPreview.title: Futile Worldly Respite and Warning Close Kin
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns that years of luxury avail nothing when torment arrives, instructs warning relatives, and refutes satanic origin.

sectionsPreview.title: Errant Poets and Exception of Righteous Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Critiques aimless, hypocritical poets followed by the astray while excepting believing poets who remember Allah and defend truth.

surahs.thematicSummary: Sulayman's kingdom, the speech of birds and ants, the Queen of Sheba (Bilqis), and signs of divine wisdom in the cosmos.

sectionsPreview.title: Guidance of the Qur'an and Musa's Fire
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents the Qur'an as glad tidings for prayerful believers and introduces Musa noticing a fire during his journey.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Nine Signs and Gratitude of Dawud
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Musa receiving the miracles of the staff and radiant hand and introduces Dawud and Sulaiman's gratitude.

sectionsPreview.title: Sulaiman's Inheritance, the Ant, and Missing Hoopoe
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Sulaiman understanding the speech of birds and the ant, his grateful prayer, and the missing hoopoe.

sectionsPreview.title: Return of the Hoopoe With Sheba's News
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the hoopoe returning to Sulaiman with a report about the prosperous Queen of Saba' and her throne.

sectionsPreview.title: Sun-Worship in Sheba and Sulaiman's Royal Letter
sectionsPreview.summary: Details the hoopoe's dismay at Sheba worshipping the sun and Sulaiman sending his letter to Queen Bilqis.

sectionsPreview.title: Bilqis Consulting Her Chiefs and Sending Gifts
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates Queen Bilqis reading Sulaiman's call to submission, consulting her chiefs, and testing him with royal gifts.

sectionsPreview.title: Refusing Gifts and Transporting Bilqis's Throne
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Sulaiman refusing Sheba's wealth, having the Queen's throne brought instantly, and testing her recognition.

sectionsPreview.title: The Crystal Palace, Bilqis's Faith, and Salih
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Bilqis entering the glass-floored palace and embracing Islam, followed by Salih confronting Thamud's nine plotters.

sectionsPreview.title: Plot Against Salih, Lut's Ruin, and Tawhid
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates the failed assassination plot against Salih, the ruin of Lut's people, and cosmic proofs of Allah's divinity.

sectionsPreview.title: Allah's Knowledge of the Unseen and Guidance
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that none knows the Unseen except Allah, refutes denial of resurrection, and consoles the Prophet.

sectionsPreview.title: Spiritual Deafness and Beast of the Earth
sectionsPreview.summary: Tells the Prophet he cannot make the spiritually blind hear, and foretells the speaking Beast before Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Gathering Deniers and Terror of the Trumpet
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the marshaling of disbelievers, highlights night and day, and describes mountains passing like clouds.

sectionsPreview.title: Security for the Righteous and Worshipping Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the safety of the righteous on Judgment Day with evildoers and concludes with devotion to Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: Musa's infancy cast upon the Nile, upbringing in Pharaoh's palace, escape to Madyan, and the ruin of proud Qarun.

sectionsPreview.title: Pharaoh's Tyranny and Empowering the Oppressed
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Pharaoh's persecution of Bani Isra'il and Allah's decree to make the oppressed leaders and inheritors.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Infancy, Restoration, and Accidental Slaying
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates casting infant Musa into the river, his adoption by Pharaoh's house, his return, and killing a Copt.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Flight and Arrival at Madyan's Well
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts a well-wisher warning Musa of Pharaoh's plot, his flight to Madyan, and meeting two modest shepherdesses.

sectionsPreview.title: Watering the Flocks and Employment Proposal
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Musa watering the women's flocks, praying in the shade, and being recommended as strong and trustworthy.

sectionsPreview.title: Marriage in Madyan and Call at Tur
sectionsPreview.summary: Details Musa's marriage contract in Madyan, his return journey, and receiving miracles at the burning bush.

sectionsPreview.title: Appointment of Harun and Pharaoh's Drowning
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Allah strengthening Musa with Harun, Pharaoh ordering Haman to build a tower, and their drowning.

sectionsPreview.title: Pharaoh's Curse and Proof of Prophethood
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents the Prophet's knowledge of Musa's history as proof of revelation and refutes those following mere desires.

sectionsPreview.title: Continuous Warnings and Believing Scriptural Scholars
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises upright scholars among the People of the Book who recognize and embrace the Qur'an as truth.

sectionsPreview.title: Double Reward and Divine Guidance Sovereignty
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises a twofold reward to patient believers from previous scriptures and affirms that Allah alone grants guidance.

sectionsPreview.title: Makkan Excuses and Justice in Destroying Towns
sectionsPreview.summary: Refutes the Makkans' fear of losing security if they embrace Islam, reminding them of the peaceful Haram.

sectionsPreview.title: Worldly Transience and Helplessness of Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts fleeting worldly ornaments with lasting reward and depicts polytheists speechless when questioned about their idols.

sectionsPreview.title: Night and Day Blessings and Arrogant Qarun
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights the alternation of night and day as divine mercy and introduces Qarun's vast treasures and rebellion.

sectionsPreview.title: Counsel to Qarun and His Earthly Ruin
sectionsPreview.summary: Records the wise counsel given to Qarun, his boastful display of wealth, and the earth swallowing him.

sectionsPreview.title: Hereafter for the Humble and Promised Return
sectionsPreview.summary: Assigns the Hereafter to the humble, promises the Prophet's return, and declares everything perishable except Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: Testing of faith in worldly life, the fragility of polytheistic reliance likened to the spider's web, and striving in Allah's path.

sectionsPreview.title: Inevitability of Trials and Reward for Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that believers will be tested to distinguish the truthful from liars and promises expiation for the righteous.

sectionsPreview.title: Parental Obedience Limits and Hypocritical Claims
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands kindness to parents unless they urge polytheism, exposes hypocrites fleeing trials, and refutes disbelievers' false offers.

sectionsPreview.title: Preaching of Nuh and Mission of Ibrahim
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Nuh's long mission before the Deluge and narrates Ibrahim's call, deliverance from fire, and migration.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Line and Destruction of Rebellious Nations
sectionsPreview.summary: Traces warnings delivered by Lut, Shu'aib, Hud, Salih, and Musa, showing how rebellious nations perished.

sectionsPreview.title: Parable of the Spider and Power of Salah
sectionsPreview.summary: Likens reliance on false deities to a fragile spider's web and commands reciting revelation and establishing prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Gracious Debate and the Unlettered Prophet
sectionsPreview.summary: Prescribes respectful dialogue with People of the Book, cites the Prophet's unlettered state, and encourages migration.

sectionsPreview.title: Universality of Death and Allah's Guaranteed Provision
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds believers that every soul tastes death, promises lofty mansions in Paradise, and guarantees Allah's universal sustenance.

sectionsPreview.title: Polytheist Inconsistency and Fleeting Worldly Life
sectionsPreview.summary: Exposes how polytheists acknowledge Allah as Creator and call upon Him at sea yet revert to idolatry.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Guidance for Those Who Strive Sincerely
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes with the assurance that Allah guides onto His paths all who strive sincerely for His sake.

surahs.thematicSummary: Prophecy of Byzantine resurgence over Sassanids, cosmic signs in marital love and diverse languages, and the innate human fitrah.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophecy of Roman Victory Over Persia
sectionsPreview.summary: Foretells that the defeated Byzantines will triumph over the Persians within a few years, gladdening the believers.

sectionsPreview.title: Superficial Worldly Knowledge and Fate of Nations
sectionsPreview.summary: Critiques people who know only the surface of worldly life while remaining heedless of the Hereafter.

sectionsPreview.title: Separation on Judgment Day and Glorifying Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the delight of Paradise with Hellfire, specifies times for glorifying Allah, and cites creation from dust.

sectionsPreview.title: Signs in Spousal Affection, Languages, and Sleep
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents marital tranquility, diversity of human languages and complexions, and restorative sleep as signs of divine wisdom.

sectionsPreview.title: Signs in Lightning and Parable of Ownership
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights lightning, reviving rain, and cosmic stability, then refutes polytheism through a parable of human ownership.

sectionsPreview.title: Adhering to the Fitrah and Avoiding Sectarianism
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands devotion to the natural faith (Fitrah) without splitting into sects and exposes human ingratitude after hardship.

sectionsPreview.title: Rights of Kin, Riba, and Widespread Corruption
sectionsPreview.summary: Enjoins giving to relatives and the needy, contrasts usury with Zakah, and warns against corruption from sins.

sectionsPreview.title: Vindication of Believers and Stages of Life
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms Allah's help to believers, compares resurrection to rain reviving earth, and traces human weakness and strength.

sectionsPreview.title: Delusion of Sinners and Command for Patience
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts sinners swearing their worldly stay lasted an hour, contrasts them with scholars, and counsels firm patience.

surahs.thematicSummary: The pedagogical wisdom of sage Luqman advising his son regarding shirk, gratitude, establishing prayer, and walking with humility.

sectionsPreview.title: The Wise Book as Guidance for the Righteous
sectionsPreview.summary: Introduces the Qur'an as wisdom and mercy for the righteous who establish prayer, pay Zakah, and believe.

sectionsPreview.title: Idle Amusements and Marvels of Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns those who purchase distracting tales to mislead people and points to the sky raised without pillars.

sectionsPreview.title: Wisdom of Luqman and Counsel Against Shirk
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Allah granting wisdom to Luqman and his opening admonition to his son that shirk is grave injustice.

sectionsPreview.title: Hardships of Motherhood and Kindness to Parents
sectionsPreview.summary: Enjoins gratitude and kindness to parents—especially the mother—while refusing obedience in associating partners with Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Luqman's Advice on Omniscience, Prayer, and Patience
sectionsPreview.summary: Continues Luqman's counsel affirming Allah's knowledge of the tiniest grain and commanding prayer, moral reform, and patience.

sectionsPreview.title: Luqman's Instructions on Humility and Modest Speech
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes Luqman's testament by forbidding arrogance and prescribing a moderate walk and a gentle, lowered voice.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Subjugation and Boundless Words of Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights Allah's blessings, the inexhaustibility of His Words, and how polytheists call on Him alone at sea.

sectionsPreview.title: Worldly Deception and Five Keys of the Unseen
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns of the Day when no parent or child avails another and lists the five unseen keys.

surahs.thematicSummary: Creation of humanity from clay and spirit, the nightly devotion of believers whose sides forsake their beds, and the Day of Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Truth of Revelation and Six-Day Cosmic Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms the Qur'an is free of doubt from the Creator who governs all cosmic affairs.

sectionsPreview.title: Perfection of Creation and Denial of Resurrection
sectionsPreview.summary: Traces human creation from clay and fluid to a proportioned soul, and refutes disbelievers doubting resurrection.

sectionsPreview.title: Angel of Death and Believers' Night Devotion
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the regret of sinners facing death with believers who forsake their beds in night prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Worldly Trials and Turning Away From Signs
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that minor worldly afflictions prompt repentance before greater torment, and condemns turning away from divine reminders.

sectionsPreview.title: Book of Musa, Patient Imams, and Past Ruins
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalls the Torah given to Musa, patient leaders among Bani Isra'il, and warnings in destroyed habitations.

sectionsPreview.title: Revival of Barren Land and Impatient Disbelievers
sectionsPreview.summary: Points to water bringing forth crops from dry land as resurrection proof and notes disbelievers' impatient challenge.

sectionsPreview.title: Futility of Late Faith on Judgment Day
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that belief on the Day of Decision will not benefit disbelievers and instructs the Prophet to wait.

surahs.thematicSummary: The Siege of Madinah (Trench), the Prophet as the supreme exemplar (Uswah Hasanah), Seal of the Prophets, and the trust (Amanah).

sectionsPreview.title: Following Revelation and Abolishing Pre-Islamic Adoption
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands following revelation, abolishes pre-Islamic adoption and Zihar claims, and declares the Prophet closer to believers than themselves.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophetic Covenant, Battle of Ahzab, and Choice
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts divine relief and exposure of hypocrites during the Trench Battle and offers the Prophet's wives simplicity.

sectionsPreview.title: The Prophet's Household and Virtuous Men and Women
sectionsPreview.summary: Addresses the special status and purification of the Prophet's household and lists ten virtues of devout believers.

sectionsPreview.title: Submission to the Prophet and Finality of Prophethood
sectionsPreview.summary: Mandates unconditional obedience to Allah and His Messenger, addresses Zaid and Zainab's marriage, and proclaims Khatm-e-Nubuwwat.

sectionsPreview.title: Abundant Remembrance and Roles of the Prophet
sectionsPreview.summary: Enjoins frequent remembrance of Allah who brings believers into light, and defines the Prophet's fivefold mission.

sectionsPreview.title: Unconsummated Divorce Ruling and Prophetic Marriages
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents the Prophet as a luminous lamp, clarifies unconsummated divorce rules, and details his specific marital rulings.

sectionsPreview.title: Etiquette of the Prophet's Homes, Durud, and Hijab
sectionsPreview.summary: Legislates privacy and Hijab in the Prophet's houses, enjoins sending blessings upon him, and mandates modest outer garments.

sectionsPreview.title: Warning to Agitators and Uprightness in Speech
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns hypocrites and rumor-mongers in Madinah, depicts followers' regrets in Hellfire, and commands Taqwa and truthful speech.

sectionsPreview.title: Bearing the Divine Trust and Final Accountability
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes with humanity undertaking the great Trust declined by the cosmos, leading to judgment and mercy.

surahs.thematicSummary: Gratitude exemplified by Dawud and Sulayman versus ungrateful ruin of the people of Sheba by the Great Dam flood (Sayl al-'Arim).

sectionsPreview.title: All-Encompassing Divine Knowledge and the Hour
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises Allah whose knowledge encompasses every atom in heaven and earth and affirms the arrival of the Hour.

sectionsPreview.title: Testimony of Scholars and Refuting Scoffers
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that people of knowledge recognize the Qur'an as truth and warns those who mock bodily resurrection.

sectionsPreview.title: Miracles of Dawud and Sulaiman and Gratitude
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes iron softened for Dawud and wind and jinn subjugated to Sulaiman, urging gratitude in action.

sectionsPreview.title: Death of Sulaiman and Flood of Saba'
sectionsPreview.summary: Shows through Sulaiman's death that jinn lack unseen knowledge, and recounts how ungrateful Sheba lost its gardens.

sectionsPreview.title: Dispersion of Sheba and Helplessness of Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates how Sheba's safe trade routes turned to ruin and refutes intercession by powerless false deities.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Prophetic Mission and Dispute of Leaders
sectionsPreview.summary: Proclaims the Prophet sent to all mankind and depicts arrogant leaders and weak followers blaming each other.

sectionsPreview.title: Criterion of Nearness to Allah and Angels' Testimony
sectionsPreview.summary: Clarifies that faith and righteous deeds bring nearness to Allah, and states that angels will disown worshippers.

sectionsPreview.title: Triumph of Revealed Truth and Late Belief
sectionsPreview.summary: Proclaims that Truth hurls down falsehood and warns of the Day when terrified disbelievers profess faith too late.

sectionsPreview.title: Barrier Between Disbelievers and Their Desires
sectionsPreview.summary: Concludes with a permanent barrier separating the disbelievers from the salvation and desires they once doubted.

surahs.thematicSummary: Allah as Originator of heavens and earth creating winged angels, human vulnerability before the Self-Sufficient Lord, and inherited scripture.

sectionsPreview.title: Allah the Originator and Enmity of Satan
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises Allah the Originator who appoints winged angels, reminds humanity of provision, and warns against Satan.

sectionsPreview.title: Beautified Evil, Revival by Winds, and True Honor
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts those blinded by adorned evil with the guided, compares resurrection to rain, and affirms Allah's honor.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Two Seas and Powerless Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights benefits from sweet and salty seas, exposes powerless idols, and contrasts spiritual blindness with sight.

sectionsPreview.title: Diversity in Nature and Awe of Scholars
sectionsPreview.summary: Compares believers and disbelievers to the living and dead, points to nature's hues, and praises God-fearing scholars.

sectionsPreview.title: Unfailing Trade of Worship and Scriptural Heirs
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises an unfailing trade to those who recite the Book, pray, and spend, and describes scriptural heirs.

sectionsPreview.title: Gratitude in Paradise and Futile Hellfire Cries
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the joyful praise of believers in eternal gardens with the rejected pleas of disbelievers in Hell.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Stewardship and Merciful Delay of Punishment
sectionsPreview.summary: Exposes the broken oaths of the Makkans, declares evil plots recoil on their makers, and highlights forbearance.

surahs.thematicSummary: The 'Heart of the Qur'an' addressing prophetic truth, the Town's envoys and Habib the carpenter, cosmic celestial mechanics, and resurrection of dry bones.

sectionsPreview.title: Confirmation of Prophethood and Warning the Heedless
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the Wise Qur'an that the Prophet is on a straight path and warns obstinate deniers.

sectionsPreview.title: Recording of Deeds and the Town's Messengers
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that Allah records all deeds and lasting footprints, and narrates three messengers sent to a city.

sectionsPreview.title: Bad Omen Accusation and Believer's Earnest Plea
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the townspeople threatening the messengers and a believing man rushing from the city's edge urging obedience.

sectionsPreview.title: Martyrdom of the Believer and Entering Paradise
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the martyr's declaration of faith, his murder by his people, and his immediate welcome into Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Destruction by One Cry and Revived Earth
sectionsPreview.summary: Narrates the instant annihilation of the town by a single blast and points to revived orchards and springs.

sectionsPreview.title: Creation in Pairs, Night, and the Sun's Orbit
sectionsPreview.summary: Glorifies Allah who created all things in pairs and governs night, day, and the sun's appointed course.

sectionsPreview.title: Phases of the Moon, Orbits, and the Ark
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights the moon's stages returning like an old palm branch, celestial orbits, and human transport in ships.

sectionsPreview.title: Means of Transport and Challenge of the Hour
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds humanity of Allah's mercy in saving travelers from drowning and warns scoffers of a single Cry.

sectionsPreview.title: Blast of the Horn and Perfect Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the sudden blowing of the Trumpet, disbelievers rushing from their graves, and absolute justice on Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Joyful Bliss of Paradise and Greeting of Peace
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the inhabitants of Paradise reclining in shade, enjoying every desire, and receiving Salam from their Lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Separation of the Guilty and Sealing of Mouths
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands the guilty to stand apart on Judgment Day, rebukes Satan-worship, and describes hands and feet testifying.

sectionsPreview.title: Reversal in Old Age and Refuting Poetry Claims
sectionsPreview.summary: Points to physical decline in old age, clears the Qur'an of being poetry, and introduces livestock blessings.

sectionsPreview.title: Subjugation of Livestock and Creation From a Drop
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights rides and food from cattle, exposes helpless idols, and rebukes man forgetting his origin from a drop.

sectionsPreview.title: Revival of Decayed Bones and Creative Command
sectionsPreview.summary: Answers the doubter holding decayed bones by affirming that the Creator revives life by simply saying 'Be.'

surahs.thematicSummary: Angelic hosts aligned in celestial ranks, Ibrahim's ultimate willingness to sacrifice his son, and salutations upon the messengers.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by the Angels Ranked in Rows
sectionsPreview.summary: Opens with solemn oaths by the angels standing in ranks, driving away evil, and reciting Allah's remembrance.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Oneness and Adornment of the Nearest Sky
sectionsPreview.summary: Proclaims that the Lord of the heavens, earth, and sunrises is One, adorning the sky with stars.

sectionsPreview.title: Guarding the Sky From Devils and Clay Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes shooting stars repelling rebellious devils from the Upper Realm and recalls human creation from sticky clay.

sectionsPreview.title: Mockery of Miracles and Day of Retribution
sectionsPreview.summary: Exposes the disbelievers dismissing signs as magic and depicts their sudden disgrace on the Day of Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Gathering Wrongdoers and Mutual Blame in Hell
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the marshaling of wrongdoers toward Hellfire where misled followers and arrogant leaders blame one another.

sectionsPreview.title: Shared Punishment and Gardens of Bliss
sectionsPreview.summary: Arrogant polytheists share in the painful punishment while Allah's chosen servants receive honored provision in Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Pure Heavenly Drink Without Any Intoxication
sectionsPreview.summary: The people of Paradise recline facing one another and enjoy a delicious, non-intoxicating white drink.

sectionsPreview.title: Spouses of Paradise and the Skeptic's Fate
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers blessed with modest companions look down upon their former skeptical acquaintance burning in Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Working for Eternal Bliss Versus Zaqqum
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are urged to strive for eternal success rather than facing the trial of the Zaqqum tree.

sectionsPreview.title: The Zaqqum Tree and Nuh's Deliverance
sectionsPreview.summary: The hideous Zaqqum tree torments the misguided, whereas Prophet Nuh and his family were saved from distress.

sectionsPreview.title: Enduring Praise and Legacy of Prophet Nuh
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah preserved Nuh's progeny as sole survivors of the Deluge and honored him among all later generations.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Pure Heart and Shattering Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: Prophet Ibrahim confronts his people's idolatry, shatters their idols, and is delivered safely from their plot.

sectionsPreview.title: Glad Tidings of a Forbearing Son
sectionsPreview.summary: Ibrahim is blessed with a patient son who willingly submits to the divine vision of sacrifice.

sectionsPreview.title: Submission of Ibrahim and Isma'il Tested
sectionsPreview.summary: When father and son both submit to Allah's command, Allah declares the dream fulfilled in trial.

sectionsPreview.title: The Great Ransom and Prophethood of Ishaq
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah ransoms Isma'il with a great sacrifice, praises Ibrahim, and grants him the prophethood of Ishaq.

sectionsPreview.title: Favors Upon Musa, Harun, and Ilyas
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah recounts His deliverance and scripture given to Musa and Harun, followed by Ilyas's call against Ba'l.

sectionsPreview.title: Arraignment of Ilyas's Deniers and His Praise
sectionsPreview.summary: Those who rejected Prophet Ilyas face arraignment in punishment, while Ilyas is honored among Allah's servants.

sectionsPreview.title: Deliverance of Lut and Departure of Yunus
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah saves Lut and destroys his sinful people, then recounts Prophet Yunus boarding the loaded ship.

sectionsPreview.title: Yunus Swallowed by the Fish and Saved
sectionsPreview.summary: After losing the cast of lots, Yunus is swallowed by a fish and saved through glorifying Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: The Gourd Tree and Yunus's Believing People
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah shelters the ailing Yunus beneath a gourd plant and accepts the faith of his hundred thousand people.

sectionsPreview.title: Refuting Pagan Myths About Angels and Jinn
sectionsPreview.summary: The Qur'an refutes false claims attributing daughters or jinn kinship to Allah while angels worship Him.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Promise of Victory for the Messengers
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah decrees ultimate triumph for His messengers and warns the polytheists of the impending punishment.

surahs.thematicSummary: Admonition through scripture, Dawud's repentance in judicial arbitration, Ayyub's endurance through illness, and Iblis's expulsion.

sectionsPreview.title: Quraysh's Rejection of Monotheism and Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: The disbelievers of Makkah marvel at the call to One God and conspire against the revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Destruction of Past Factions Who Denied Messengers
sectionsPreview.summary: Powerful ancient nations from Nuh and 'Ad to Pharaoh and Thamud incurred punishment for belying prophets.

sectionsPreview.title: The Uninterrupted Cry and Pagan Mockery
sectionsPreview.summary: The disbelievers mockingly demand their share of punishment before the Day of Reckoning when the Cry sounds.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophet Dawud's Devotion and Glorification with Nature
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet is enjoined to be patient and remember Dawud, with whom mountains and birds glorified Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Dawud's Strong Kingdom and the Two Litigants
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah grants Dawud wisdom and decisive speech, testing him when two litigants climb over his sanctuary wall.

sectionsPreview.title: Dispute of the Ewes and Dawud's Repentance
sectionsPreview.summary: Hearing the complaint about ninety-nine ewes, Dawud realizes he is being tested and falls in penitent prostration.

sectionsPreview.title: Forgiveness of Dawud and Just Governance
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah forgives Dawud, grants him nearness, and commands him to judge with truth rather than personal desire.

sectionsPreview.title: Purposeful Creation and the Blessed Book
sectionsPreview.summary: The heavens and earth were not created in vain, and the blessed Qur'an was revealed for reflection.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophet Sulaiman and the Noble Horses
sectionsPreview.summary: Sulaiman's devotion to Allah's remembrance is demonstrated when evening inspection of swift horses engages his attention.

sectionsPreview.title: Sulaiman's Trial and Subjugation of Wind
sectionsPreview.summary: Tested on his throne, Sulaiman prays for an unmatched kingdom, receiving command over wind and jinn builders.

sectionsPreview.title: Sulaiman's Gift and Ayyub's Healing Spring
sectionsPreview.summary: Sulaiman is granted unconditional authority, and Prophet Ayyub is healed and restored in family after patient endurance.

sectionsPreview.title: Fulfilling Ayyub's Oath and Remembering the Patriarchs
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah guides the enduring Ayyub to fulfill his oath gently and praises the vision of Ibrahim's line.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophets Mindful of the Eternal Home
sectionsPreview.summary: Chosen prophets were distinguished by constant remembrance of the Hereafter, where open-doored gardens await the God-fearing.

sectionsPreview.title: Bliss in Paradise and Quarrels in Hellfire
sectionsPreview.summary: While believers enjoy unending bliss, the transgressors in Hell curse one another and regret mocking the righteous.

sectionsPreview.title: Heavenly Debate, Adam's Creation, and Iblis's Pride
sectionsPreview.summary: Revelation informs the Prophet of the angels prostrating before Adam upon his creation while Iblis arrogantly refused.

sectionsPreview.title: Arrogance of Iblis and Universal Qur'anic Advice
sectionsPreview.summary: Iblis is cursed and vows to mislead humanity except Allah's chosen servants, concluding with the Qur'an's warning.

surahs.thematicSummary: Sincere monotheism, the famous verse of boundless hope for transgressing souls (39:53), and entry of righteous crowds into Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Sincere Devotion to Allah Versus Intercessors
sectionsPreview.summary: The Book calls for exclusive devotion to Allah and refutes those who worship idols claiming nearness.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Oneness, Cosmic Order, and Human Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah transcends having offspring, governs the sun and moon, and forms humanity through three stages in wombs.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Self-Sufficiency and Sincere Nocturnal Worship
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah needs no one yet approves of gratitude, contrasting the devout nocturnal worshipper with worshippers of Taghut.

sectionsPreview.title: Following the Best Word and Open Hearts
sectionsPreview.summary: Glad tidings are given to those who follow the best word and whose hearts open to Islam.

sectionsPreview.title: Impact of the Qur'an and Two Masters
sectionsPreview.summary: The Qur'an softens the hearts of the God-fearing, illustrates monotheism by parable, and reminds all of mortality.

sectionsPreview.title: Disputes on Judgment Day and Allah's Sufficiency
sectionsPreview.summary: Humanity will settle its disputes before Allah, who suffices His servant and reveals the Book for guidance.

sectionsPreview.title: Souls in Death and Sleep and Intercession
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah controls souls during death and sleep, owns all intercession, and tests mankind by expanding and restricting provision.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Call to Repentance and Divine Mercy
sectionsPreview.summary: Transgressing servants are told never to despair of Allah's mercy and to repent before sudden punishment arrives.

sectionsPreview.title: Consequences of Arrogance and Majesty of Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Deniers fail to appreciate Allah's majesty, though the entire earth and rolled-up heavens rest in His grip.

sectionsPreview.title: Blowing the Horn and Processions to Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Upon the Trumpet's blast, judgment is passed as disbelievers are driven to Hell and believers enter Paradise.

surahs.thematicSummary: First of the Hawamim surahs; Allah's forgiveness and severe reckoning, the secret Believer in Pharaoh's court pleading for Musa.

sectionsPreview.title: Revelation of the Book from the All-Mighty
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah Ghafir opens by affirming the Qur'an as a revelation from Allah, the Mighty and All-Knowing.

sectionsPreview.title: Forgiver of Sins and Fate of Deniers
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah forgives sins and accepts repentance, yet seizes arrogant disputants just as He destroyed previous rejecting nations.

sectionsPreview.title: Supplication of Throne-Bearers and Regret in Hell
sectionsPreview.summary: The angels bearing the Throne pray for the believers' forgiveness while disbelievers confess their sins in Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Sovereignty on Judgment Day and Musa's Mission
sectionsPreview.summary: On the Day when nothing is hidden, sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, who sent Musa with signs.

sectionsPreview.title: Pharaoh's Plot and the Believer's Defense
sectionsPreview.summary: When Pharaoh plots to kill Musa, a believing man from Pharaoh's family courageously warns his people.

sectionsPreview.title: Day of Mutual Calling and Yusuf's Signs
sectionsPreview.summary: The believer from Pharaoh's family warns of Resurrection Day and recalls their earlier doubts regarding Prophet Yusuf.

sectionsPreview.title: Pharaoh's Arrogance and Call to Salvation
sectionsPreview.summary: While Pharaoh mocks heavenly ascension, the believing man contrasts fleeting worldly life with the permanent Hereafter.

sectionsPreview.title: Entrusting Affairs to Allah and Pharaoh's Ruin
sectionsPreview.summary: The believing man entrusts his affair to Allah, who protects him and encompasses Pharaoh's people in ruin.

sectionsPreview.title: Torment of the Grave and Divine Support
sectionsPreview.summary: Pharaoh's people face the Fire morning and evening before Judgment Day, while Allah supports His messengers.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Creation and Command to Supplicate
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah exposes the hollow pride of disputants, points to cosmic creation, and promises to answer supplications.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Creation and Shackles for Deniers
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah's favors in night, day, and human creation demand pure monotheism, whereas deniers face chains in Hell.

sectionsPreview.title: Vanishing of False Deities on Judgment Day
sectionsPreview.summary: Cast into boiling water and Fire, the polytheists confess that the false gods they invoked have vanished.

sectionsPreview.title: Punishment for Earthly Arrogance and Historical Lessons
sectionsPreview.summary: Arrogant exultation on earth leads to eternal Hellfire, and travelers are urged to reflect on past ruins.

sectionsPreview.title: Futility of Faith Professed During Punishment
sectionsPreview.summary: Ancient nations who boasted of worldly knowledge found their late declaration of faith useless under punishment.

surahs.thematicSummary: Exposition on divine revelation, cosmic signs in creation, and the steadfast perseverance required in calling humanity to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Elaborated Arabic Qur'an from the All-Merciful
sectionsPreview.summary: The Book is revealed by the All-Merciful with verses clearly explained in Arabic for people of understanding.

sectionsPreview.title: Stubbornness of Disbelievers and Call to Tawhid
sectionsPreview.summary: Though polytheists claim their hearts are veiled, the Prophet proclaims he is a human warner preaching Tawhid.

sectionsPreview.title: Woe to Deniers of Zakah and Hereafter
sectionsPreview.summary: Polytheists who withhold Zakah and deny the Hereafter are rebuked for disbelieving in the Earth's Creator.

sectionsPreview.title: Six-Day Cosmic Creation and Arrogance of 'Ad
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah proportioned the earth's sustenance and adorned the seven heavens, warning Makkans with arrogant 'Ad and Thamud.

sectionsPreview.title: The Furious Wind and Testimony of Skins
sectionsPreview.summary: After recounting the wind that destroyed 'Ad, the Qur'an depicts sinners' ears, eyes, and skins testifying.

sectionsPreview.title: Disrupting Recitation Versus Angels Greeting the Steadfast
sectionsPreview.summary: Disbelievers making noise during Qur'anic recitation face disgrace, while angels descend with glad tidings upon steadfast believers.

sectionsPreview.title: Calling to Allah and Repelling Evil
sectionsPreview.summary: The best speech is calling to Allah, repelling evil with goodness, and prostrating only to the Creator.

sectionsPreview.title: Tireless Angelic Glorification and Reviving Dead Earth
sectionsPreview.summary: Angels glorify Allah without weariness, reviving rain proves resurrection, and those who distort Allah's verses are warned.

sectionsPreview.title: Infallibility of the Qur'an and Human Fickleness
sectionsPreview.summary: Falsehood cannot approach the Qur'an, yet ungrateful humans swing between despair in hardship and pride in prosperity.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Signs in Horizons and Human Souls
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah will manifest His signs across the universe and within human beings until the Qur'an's truth is clear.

surahs.thematicSummary: Unity of divine message, ethical conduct of the community based on consultation (Shura), and absolute divine transcendence.

sectionsPreview.title: Unity of Revelation and Allah as Patron
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah reveals the Arabic Qur'an to warn Makkah, reminding humanity that He alone is the true Patron.

sectionsPreview.title: Shared Religion of Prophets and Later Schisms
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah ordained the same foundational faith for all prophets, though later people divided out of mutual jealousy.

sectionsPreview.title: Steadfast Invitation to Truth and the Hour
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet is commanded to remain steadfast, judge justly among people, and warn disputants of the Hour.

sectionsPreview.title: Harvest of the Hereafter and Prophetic Sincerity
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah multiplies the reward of those seeking the Hereafter and commands the Prophet to ask no wage.

sectionsPreview.title: Acceptance of Repentance and Measured Sustenance
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah accepts repentance from His servants, proportions sustenance to prevent mischief, and sends reviving rain after despair.

sectionsPreview.title: Signs in Seas and Superiority of Hereafter
sectionsPreview.summary: Human afflictions stem from their own deeds though Allah pardons much, and eternal rewards excel worldly enjoyment.

sectionsPreview.title: Mutual Consultation, Forgiveness, and Just Retribution
sectionsPreview.summary: True believers avoid major sins, conduct affairs by consultation, and prioritize forgiveness even when entitled to retaliation.

sectionsPreview.title: Gift of Offspring and Modes of Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah grants sons, daughters, or barrenness as He wills, and communicates through inspiration, a veil, or angels.

surahs.thematicSummary: Contrast between fleeting worldly vanity (gold and adornments) and everlasting heavenly honors, rebutting false deities and polytheistic conjecture.

sectionsPreview.title: Arabic Qur'an in the Preserved Mother Book
sectionsPreview.summary: The clear Arabic Qur'an is exalted and full of wisdom within the Mother of the Book.

sectionsPreview.title: Persistence of Revelation and Acknowledging the Creator
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah does not withhold revelation despite transgression, noting that even polytheists admit Allah created the cosmos.

sectionsPreview.title: Subjugation of Mounts and Supplication of Travel
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah created all pairs and provided ships and cattle so believers praise Him when embarking on journeys.

sectionsPreview.title: Hypocrisy of Attributing Daughters to the All-Merciful
sectionsPreview.summary: Pagans are rebuked for attributing daughters to Allah while their own faces darken at a daughter's birth.

sectionsPreview.title: Blind Imitation Refuted by Ibrahim's Disavowal
sectionsPreview.summary: The polytheists' excuse of blindly following forefathers is contrasted with Ibrahim's disavowal of his people's idols.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Lasting Word and Worldly Objections
sectionsPreview.summary: Ibrahim left monotheism among his posterity, whereas Makkah's elite objected that revelation bypassed wealthy town chiefs.

sectionsPreview.title: Distribution of Livelihood and Worthlessness of Gold
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah alone distributes prophethood and livelihood, and worldly silver or gold is mere fleeting enjoyment.

sectionsPreview.title: Satanic Companions and Holding Fast to Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: Whoever turns blind to Allah's remembrance is assigned a devil companion whom he will regret on Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: The Qur'an as Honor and Past Messengers
sectionsPreview.summary: The Qur'an is a source of honor and accountability, and all past messengers taught pure monotheism.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Signs and Pharaoh's Arrogant Boasts
sectionsPreview.summary: Pharaoh and his chiefs broke their promises after each plague and mocked Musa's lack of gold bracelets.

sectionsPreview.title: Drowning of Pharaoh's Host as a Warning
sectionsPreview.summary: Pharaoh befooled his sinful people into obeying him until Allah drowned them all as a lasting example.

sectionsPreview.title: Pagan Disputation Over 'Isa's Servant Status
sectionsPreview.summary: When the polytheists cited 'Isa in contentious debate, Allah clarified that 'Isa was a favored servant.

sectionsPreview.title: 'Isa as a Sign of the Hour
sectionsPreview.summary: Prophet 'Isa's descent is a sign of the approaching Hour, and his message called to worship Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Enmity of Worldly Friends and Final Recompense
sectionsPreview.summary: On Judgment Day all friendships not based on piety turn to enmity, as believers enter eternal Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: The Prophet's Complaint and Bidding Peace
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah hears the Prophet's grief over his people's disbelief and instructs him to turn away gracefully.

surahs.thematicSummary: The blessed night of revelation, warning of retribution symbolized by impending cosmic smoke, and the demise of Pharaoh's tyranny.

sectionsPreview.title: Oath by the Clear and Manifest Book
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah Ad-Dukhan opens with the isolated letters Ha Mim and an oath by the manifest Book.

sectionsPreview.title: Revelation in the Blessed Night and Smoke
sectionsPreview.summary: The Qur'an descended on a blessed night of decree, and stubborn deniers are warned of visible smoke.

sectionsPreview.title: Musa's Night Exodus and Pharaoh's Drowning
sectionsPreview.summary: Musa leads the believers out by night while Pharaoh's army drowns, leaving behind gardens and treasures.

sectionsPreview.title: Unmourned Ruin of Pharaoh and Israel's Deliverance
sectionsPreview.summary: Neither heaven nor earth wept over Pharaoh's drowned host as Allah delivered the Children of Israel.

sectionsPreview.title: Choosing Bani Isra'il and Denial of Resurrection
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah recalls His past favors upon Bani Isra'il and quotes the Makkans' denial of life after death.

sectionsPreview.title: Demand to Revive Forefathers and Purposeful Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Disbelievers challenge believers to bring back their dead fathers, forgetting how the people of Tubba' perished.

sectionsPreview.title: The Day of Decision and Boiling Zaqqum
sectionsPreview.summary: On the Day of Decision, sinners are fed the boiling Zaqqum tree and scalded with hot water.

sectionsPreview.title: The God-Fearing in Gardens and Silk Attire
sectionsPreview.summary: In contrast to Hellfire, the God-fearing dwell securely amid gardens and springs, arrayed in fine silk.

sectionsPreview.title: Companions of Paradise and Freedom from Death
sectionsPreview.summary: The righteous are wedded to pure companions and never taste death again in eternal Paradise.

surahs.thematicSummary: Signs of Allah in heavens and earth, rebuke of materialistic skepticism, and the scene of all nations kneeling before the divine tribunal.

sectionsPreview.title: Revelation from the All-Mighty and All-Wise
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah Al-Jathiyah commences by affirming the divine origin of the Book from Allah, the Mighty and Wise.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Signs of Faith and Arrogant Mockers
sectionsPreview.summary: Signs across the heavens, earth, and winds prove Allah's Oneness, while woe awaits arrogant mockers of revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Punishment of Deniers and Subjugation of Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Hellfire awaits the deniers while Allah reminds humanity how He subjugated the sea and cosmos for them.

sectionsPreview.title: Pardoning Disbelievers and Schisms of Bani Isra'il
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are told to pardon disbelievers, while the Children of Israel differed only after receiving clear knowledge.

sectionsPreview.title: Following the Shari'ah and Moral Justice
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet is commanded to follow the revealed Shari'ah strictly, as evildoers and believers are never equal.

sectionsPreview.title: Worshipping Desires and Attributing Death to Time
sectionsPreview.summary: Those who take desires as their god and claim only time destroys them will lose on Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Every Nation Kneeling Before Its Record
sectionsPreview.summary: On the Day when every community kneels before its record, believers attain mercy and deniers face disgrace.

surahs.thematicSummary: The reality of resurrection, filial duty to parents, the warning delivered to the people of 'Ad in the dunes, and the faith of listening jinn.

sectionsPreview.title: Helplessness of Idols and Refuting Forgery Claims
sectionsPreview.summary: Idols cannot answer prayers and will reject their worshippers on Judgment Day, while Allah witnesses the Qur'an's truth.

sectionsPreview.title: Following Revelation Confirmed by Earlier Scripture
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet declares he is no novelty among messengers, following only revelation attested by a witness from Israel.

sectionsPreview.title: Elitist Scorn and Confirmation of Musa's Book
sectionsPreview.summary: Arrogant disbelievers dismiss Islam because the poor embraced it first, though the Qur'an confirms Musa's Torah.

sectionsPreview.title: Steadfastness in Faith and Kindness to Parents
sectionsPreview.summary: Steadfast believers have no fear, and mankind is enjoined to honor parents and pray gratefully at forty.

sectionsPreview.title: Reward of the Righteous Versus Rebellious Offspring
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah accepts the best deeds of dutiful believers, contrasting them with the child who spurns his parents' faith.

sectionsPreview.title: Exhausting Worldly Pleasures and Destruction of 'Ad
sectionsPreview.summary: Disbelievers who exhausted their pleasures in worldly life are warned with Hud's preaching before the wind destroyed 'Ad.

sectionsPreview.title: Jinn Listening Attentively to the Qur'an
sectionsPreview.summary: A group of jinn listen silently to the Prophet's recitation and return to their people as warners.

sectionsPreview.title: Preaching of Jinn and Resolute Prophetic Patience
sectionsPreview.summary: The jinn urge their people to answer Allah's caller, and the Prophet must emulate the resolute messengers.

surahs.thematicSummary: Delineation between belief and disbelief, ethical rules of combat and treatment of captives, and the spiritual hypocrisy hindering righteous sacrifice.

sectionsPreview.title: Nullifying Disbelievers' Deeds and Battlefield Injunctions
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah renders obstructers' deeds vain, expiates believers' sins, and lays down rules regarding combat and war captives.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Support for Believers and Ruin of Deniers
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah guides and stabilizes those who help His cause, while frustrating the deeds of those hating revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Rivers of Paradise Versus Boiling Hellfire
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers enjoy pure rivers of water, milk, wine, and honey in Paradise while deniers drink boiling water.

sectionsPreview.title: Seeking Forgiveness and Cowardice of Hypocrites
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are commanded to seek forgiveness, while hypocrites faint with terror when a Surah enjoins fighting.

sectionsPreview.title: Locked Hearts of Hypocrites and Angelic Punishment
sectionsPreview.summary: Those who sever kinship ties and collude with enemies have locked hearts and face angels striking them.

sectionsPreview.title: Exposing Secret Grudges and Testing Through Jihad
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah exposes the malice of hypocrites through their tone of speech and tests believers to distinguish strivers.

sectionsPreview.title: Guarding Deeds from Nullification and Staying Courageous
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are warned not to nullify their deeds by opposing the Messenger and urged never to falter.

sectionsPreview.title: Fleeting Worldly Life and Warning Against Miserliness
sectionsPreview.summary: Worldly life is mere play and pastime, and those who withhold in miserliness only harm themselves.

surahs.thematicSummary: Celebrating the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as a clear moral victory, divine reassurance (Sakinah) to believers, and the nobility of the Prophet's companions.

sectionsPreview.title: The Manifest Victory of Hudaibiyah and Forgiveness
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah proclaims the Treaty of Hudaibiyah a manifest victory through which He completes His favor and support.

sectionsPreview.title: Tranquility, Pledge of Allegiance, and Lagging Bedouins
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah sent tranquility upon the believers who pledged allegiance and exposed the excuses of lagging Bedouins.

sectionsPreview.title: Exclusion of Laggards and Pledge Under the Tree
sectionsPreview.summary: Laggards from Hudaibiyah are barred from Khaibar's spoils, while Allah is pleased with those pledging under the tree.

sectionsPreview.title: Spoils of Khaibar and Allah's Unchanging Sunnah
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah rewards the faithful with Khaibar's spoils, promises future victories, and affirms His unchanging law of victory.

sectionsPreview.title: Restraining Hands at Makkah and Word of Piety
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah prevented armed clash at Hudaibiyah to protect concealed believers in Makkah and honored Muslims with piety.

sectionsPreview.title: Fulfillment of the Dream and Noble Companions
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah confirms the Prophet's dream of entering the Sacred Mosque peacefully and praises his Companions in scripture.

surahs.thematicSummary: The constitutional ethics of the Muslim community: reverence before the Prophet, verifying news, brotherly reconciliation, prohibiting backbiting, and human universal equality under Taqwa.

sectionsPreview.title: Reverence for the Prophet and Lowering Voices
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers must never advance ahead of Allah and His Messenger and must lower their voices before him.

sectionsPreview.title: Respecting the Prophet's Chambers and Verifying News
sectionsPreview.summary: Calling the Prophet impatiently from outside his chambers is reproved, and reports from sinners must be verified.

sectionsPreview.title: Endearing Faith and Reconciling Fighting Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah endeared faith to believers and declared all believers brothers who must reconcile warring factions with justice.

sectionsPreview.title: Prohibition of Mockery, Suspicion, Spying, and Backbiting
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are strictly forbidden from mocking others, using offensive nicknames, entertaining ill suspicion, spying, or backbiting.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Equality in Piety and True Faith
sectionsPreview.summary: Humanity is created from one pair where honor lies in piety, distinguishing outward submission from true faith.
