surahs.thematicSummary: Majestic contemplation of creation and bodily resurrection, divine intimacy closer than the jugular vein, the recording angels, and the trumpet of judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Wonder at Resurrection and Proofs in Nature
sectionsPreview.summary: Disbelievers marvel at resurrection after death, so Allah points to the flawless sky, mountains, and reviving rain.

sectionsPreview.title: Past Deniers and Ease of Second Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Ancient communities were destroyed for denying messengers, and Allah was never wearied by the first creation.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Closeness and the Two Recording Angels
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah knows the whispers of the human soul and is closer than the jugular vein as angels record.

sectionsPreview.title: Stupor of Death and Sharp Sight at Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: The stupor of death and Trumpet's blast bring every soul with a driver and witness, sharpening sight.

sectionsPreview.title: Presenting the Record and the Devil's Disavowal
sectionsPreview.summary: The recording angel presents the book of deeds, stubborn disbelievers enter Hell, and their devil companion disowns them.

sectionsPreview.title: Silence in Allah's Court and Approaching Paradise
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah silences quarrelling in His court as Hell asks for more and Paradise draws near the God-fearing.

sectionsPreview.title: Entering Paradise in Peace and Past Lessons
sectionsPreview.summary: Those who feared the All-Merciful unseen enter eternal peace, while stronger past generations found no escape from ruin.

sectionsPreview.title: Lesson for Attentive Hearts and Constant Glorification
sectionsPreview.summary: Creation of the cosmos in six days without fatigue instructs attentive hearts, and the Prophet must glorify Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: The Caller's Cry and Exhorting with the Qur'an
sectionsPreview.summary: On the Day when the earth splits open for gathering, the Prophet's duty is reminding with the Qur'an.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oaths by cosmological forces confirming judgment, the visitation of angels to Ibrahim, and the overarching purpose of jinn and mankind: to worship Allah alone.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Winds Affirming the Promised Recompense
sectionsPreview.summary: Swearing by the dust-scattering winds, rain clouds, ships, and angels, Allah affirms that the Recompense is true.

sectionsPreview.title: Doom of Conjecturers and Night Devotion
sectionsPreview.summary: Heedless conjecturers face the Fire, whereas the God-fearing prayed at night and sought forgiveness at dawn.

sectionsPreview.title: Rights of the Needy and Signs Within Ourselves
sectionsPreview.summary: The righteous recognized a right in their wealth for the needy, and signs abound within human selves.

sectionsPreview.title: Heavenly Sustenance and Arrival of Ibrahim's Guests
sectionsPreview.summary: Human sustenance is decreed in heaven as surely as speech, followed by angelic guests greeting Prophet Ibrahim.

sectionsPreview.title: Ibrahim's Hospitality and Tidings of a Son
sectionsPreview.summary: When the angelic guests refrain from eating the calf, they calm Ibrahim and announce a knowledgeable son.

sectionsPreview.title: Angels' Mission to Lut and Past Nations' Ruin
sectionsPreview.summary: The angels reveal their mission to rain marked stones upon Lut's people, followed by reminders of past nations.

sectionsPreview.title: Expanding Sky and Purpose of Human Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah built the expanding sky, created pairs, and created jinn and humanity solely to worship Him.

sectionsPreview.title: Allah the All-Sustainer and Woe to Disbelievers
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah seeks no sustenance from creation since He is the Strong Sustainer, and woe awaits wrongdoers.

surahs.thematicSummary: Solemn oaths by Mount Sinai and the Inhabited House (Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur), the bliss of the righteous joined by their families in Paradise, and refuting skeptical accusations.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Mount Tur and Inscribed Scroll
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah At-Tur opens with solemn oaths by Mount Tur and a Book inscribed on an unrolled scroll.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by the Populated House and Flaming Sea
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah swears by Al-Bait-ul-Ma'mur in the heavens, the elevated canopy of the sky, and the blazing sea.

sectionsPreview.title: Inevitable Punishment and Rewards of the God-Fearing
sectionsPreview.summary: When the sky trembles, deniers are shoved into Hellfire while the God-fearing recline in Gardens of Bliss.

sectionsPreview.title: Reunion of Believing Families and Refuting Slanders
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah unites believing offspring with their righteous parents in Paradise and refutes pagan accusations through probing questions.

sectionsPreview.title: Demolishing Polytheist Claims and Warning of Punishment
sectionsPreview.summary: Incisive questions expose the absurdity of polytheism and warn wrongdoers of punishment before and on Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Patience Under Allah's Care and Night Glorification
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet is comforted that he is before Allah's Eyes and instructed to glorify his Lord at night.

surahs.thematicSummary: The supreme celestial vision of the Prophet during the Ascension (Mi'raj) at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and the futility of polytheistic idolatry.

sectionsPreview.title: Veracity of Prophetic Revelation Taught by Jibril
sectionsPreview.summary: Swearing by the setting star, Allah testifies that the Prophet speaks only pure revelation taught by Jibril.

sectionsPreview.title: Jibril's Manifestation on the Upper Horizon
sectionsPreview.summary: Endowed with mighty faculties, angel Jibril appeared on the highest horizon and drew near to convey revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophetic Vision at Sidrat-ul-Muntaha During Ascension
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet's heart did not err in what he saw, beholding Jibril again near Sidrat-ul-Muntaha and Jannat-ul-Ma'wa.

sectionsPreview.title: Unwavering Prophetic Sight and Futility of Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet's gaze never swerved while beholding great signs, whereas Lat, 'Uzza, and Manat are exposed as false.

sectionsPreview.title: Following Conjecture and Shunning Self-Righteous Claims
sectionsPreview.summary: Idolaters follow only invented names and conjecture, and believers must never claim purity for their own souls.

sectionsPreview.title: Teachings of the Scriptures of Musa and Ibrahim
sectionsPreview.summary: He who stops giving is reminded of Musa and Ibrahim's scrolls that each bears his own burden.

sectionsPreview.title: Reward for Personal Effort and Divine Power
sectionsPreview.summary: Every human receives the full recompense of his own striving, and to Allah belong life, death, and resurrection.

sectionsPreview.title: Lord of Sirius and Destroyer of Rebellious Nations
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah is the Giver of wealth, Lord of Sirius, and Destroyer of ancient 'Ad, Thamud, and Nuh's people.

sectionsPreview.title: Approach of the Imminent Hour of Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalling the punishment that covered the overturned cities, the Qur'an warns that the Imminent Hour has drawn near.

sectionsPreview.title: Warning Against Heedless Laughter and Prostration Command
sectionsPreview.summary: Those who laugh heedlessly at the Qur'an instead of weeping are commanded to prostrate and worship Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: The miraculous cleaving of the moon, warnings from ancient destroyed civilizations, and the fourfold refrain: 'And We have indeed made the Quran easy for remembrance.'

sectionsPreview.title: Splitting of the Moon and Stubborn Denial
sectionsPreview.summary: The Hour has drawn near and the moon split asunder, yet disbelievers call every sign transient magic.

sectionsPreview.title: Emerging from Graves Like Scattered Locusts
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet is told to turn from heedless deniers until the hard Day when they emerge like locusts.

sectionsPreview.title: Rejection of Prophet Nuh and the Deluge
sectionsPreview.summary: When Nuh's people called him a madman, Allah answered his prayer with torrential rain and gushing springs.

sectionsPreview.title: Salvation of Nuh's Ark and Easy Qur'an
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah carried Nuh on a vessel of planks and nails and declares the Qur'an easy for remembrance.

sectionsPreview.title: Destruction of 'Ad, Thamud, Lut's People, and Pharaoh
sectionsPreview.summary: The fates of 'Ad, Thamud, Lut's people, and Pharaoh warn the Makkans that they have no immunity.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Predestination and the Seat of Truth
sectionsPreview.summary: Everything is created in due measure and recorded, while the God-fearing dwell near the Omnipotent Sovereign.

surahs.thematicSummary: A rhythmic choral masterpiece enumerating cosmic favors and paradisiacal wonders, punctuated thirty-one times by: 'Which of the favors of your Lord will you twain deny?'

sectionsPreview.title: Teaching the Qur'an, Speech, and Cosmic Calculation
sectionsPreview.summary: The All-Merciful taught the Qur'an, created man and taught him speech, and bound the sun and moon.

sectionsPreview.title: Prostration of Plants and Weighing with Justice
sectionsPreview.summary: Plants and trees submit to Allah, who raised the sky and established the scale for just weighing.

sectionsPreview.title: Earthly Bounties and Refrain on Divine Favors
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah spread the earth with fruits, date-palms, grain, and flowers, asking jinn and mankind which bounty they deny.

sectionsPreview.title: Creation of Man and Jinn and Two Seas
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah created man from ringing clay, jinn from smokeless fire, and placed a barrier between meeting seas.

sectionsPreview.title: Pearls, Towering Ships, and Mortality of Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Pearls emerge from the seas where ships sail, and all on earth perishes except your Lord's Countenance.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Dependence and Inability to Escape Realms
sectionsPreview.summary: All in heaven and earth beseech Allah daily, and none can escape across cosmic realms at Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Seizing the Guilty and Two Heavenly Gardens
sectionsPreview.summary: Sinners are seized by forelocks and feet, whereas whoever feared standing before his Lord receives two gardens.

sectionsPreview.title: Abundant Fruits, Brocade Couches, and Further Gardens
sectionsPreview.summary: The first two gardens abound in paired fruits and silk-lined couches, followed by two more lush gardens.

sectionsPreview.title: Guarded Companions and Glorifying the Majestic Lord
sectionsPreview.summary: The inhabitants recline on green cushions with modest companions in pavilions, praising the Lord of Majesty.

surahs.thematicSummary: The cataclysm of the Last Day dividing humankind into three classes: the Foremost in Faith (Al-Sabiqun), the Companions of the Right, and the Companions of the Left.

sectionsPreview.title: The Inevitable Event and Crumbling of Mountains
sectionsPreview.summary: When the Inevitable Event of Resurrection occurs, the earth will be shaken and mountains reduced to dust.

sectionsPreview.title: Division of Humanity into Three Categories
sectionsPreview.summary: Humanity will be divided into the People of the Right, the Left, and the Foremost near Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Gold-Woven Thrones and Goblets for the Foremost
sectionsPreview.summary: The Foremost recline on gold-woven thrones served by immortal youths bearing goblets of pure drink and fruit.

sectionsPreview.title: Peace for the Foremost and Thornless Lote-Trees
sectionsPreview.summary: The Foremost enjoy bird meat, pure companions, and peace greetings, while the Right dwell amid thornless lote-trees.

sectionsPreview.title: Clustered Banana Trees, Shade, and Flowing Water
sectionsPreview.summary: The People of the Right are blessed with layered banana trees, spreading shade, and continuously flowing water.

sectionsPreview.title: Uninterrupted Fruits and Elevated Couches in Paradise
sectionsPreview.summary: They enjoy abundant fruits that are neither seasonal nor forbidden while reclining upon elevated couches.

sectionsPreview.title: Special Creation of Companions for the Right
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah creates the women of Paradise anew as devoted, age-matched companions for the People of the Right.

sectionsPreview.title: Torment of the Left and Four Creative Proofs
sectionsPreview.summary: After describing the torment of the Left, Allah proves resurrection through human birth, agriculture, rain, and fire.

sectionsPreview.title: Fire as Reminder and Oath by Stars
sectionsPreview.summary: Earthly fire serves as a reminder and traveler's benefit, followed by an oath by setting stars.

sectionsPreview.title: The Noble Qur'an in a Protected Book
sectionsPreview.summary: The oath affirms that this is a Noble Qur'an preserved in a protected Book, touched by the purified.

sectionsPreview.title: Helplessness at Death and Three Final Destinations
sectionsPreview.summary: Deniers are helpless when a dying person's soul reaches the throat, leading to rest, peace, or Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Truth of Certainty and Glorifying the Lord
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah Al-Waqi'ah concludes by declaring these realities the truth of certainty and commanding glorification of the Lord.

surahs.thematicSummary: The supreme attributes of Allah, spending in times of difficulty vs ease, the light of believers on the Day of Judgment, and the creation of iron containing mighty power and human benefit.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Glorification, Omniscience, and Divine Sovereignty
sectionsPreview.summary: All in heaven and earth glorify Allah, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, and All-Knowing.

sectionsPreview.title: Spending as Trustees and Advancing Goodly Loans
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are urged to spend from wealth entrusted to them, with higher rank for spending before Victory.

sectionsPreview.title: Light of Believers Versus Barrier Against Hypocrites
sectionsPreview.summary: On Judgment Day believers walk by their light while a wall shuts out hypocrites, urging humble hearts.

sectionsPreview.title: Rank of Truthful and Racing to Forgiveness
sectionsPreview.summary: True believers hold the rank of Siddiqs, worldly life is fleeting vegetation, and believers must race to Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Predestined Calamities and Sending Book, Balance, and Iron
sectionsPreview.summary: All calamities are pre-recorded so believers neither despair nor boast, and Allah sent scripture, justice, and iron.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophethood, Invented Monasticism, and Double Mercy
sectionsPreview.summary: Prophethood continued to 'Isa whose followers invented monasticism, while believers in Muhammad receive a double share of mercy.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Bounty Exclusively in Allah's Hand
sectionsPreview.summary: The People of the Book hold no monopoly over Allah's grace, which He bestows as He wills.

surahs.thematicSummary: Divine hearing answering the petition of a wronged woman, nullifying pagan domestic oppression (Zihar), and condemning conspiratorial whispers.

sectionsPreview.title: Hearing the Pleading Woman and Condemning Zihar
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah hears the plea of Khaulah regarding her husband and condemns the pagan custom of Zihar.

sectionsPreview.title: Legal Expiation Prescribed for Retracting Zihar
sectionsPreview.summary: A husband retracting Zihar must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty needy persons.

sectionsPreview.title: Disgrace of Opponents and Omnipresent Divine Knowledge
sectionsPreview.summary: Those opposing Allah face humiliation, and no secret counsel of three or five occurs without Allah present.

sectionsPreview.title: Prohibition of Sinful Whisperings That Grieve Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Hypocrites are rebuked for whispering sin and sedition, and believers must converse privately only in piety.

sectionsPreview.title: Assembly Etiquette, Scholarly Rank, and Private Consultation
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers must make room in assemblies, know Allah elevates scholars, and observe etiquette in private prophetic consultations.

sectionsPreview.title: Party of Satan Versus Party of Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Hypocrites allying with Allah's enemies belong to Satan's losing party, whereas true believers love no opponent of Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: The exile of Banu Nadir, ethical distribution of community resources (Fay'), selfless fraternal sacrifice of the Ansar, and the sublime Beautiful Names of Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Expulsion of Banu Nadir from Their Fortresses
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah cast terror into the hearts of Banu Nadir, expelling them from their strongholds for opposing Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Cutting Palm Trees and Spoils Without Combat
sectionsPreview.summary: Cutting Banu Nadir's palm trees occurred by divine leave, and peacefully gained spoils belong to Allah's Messenger.

sectionsPreview.title: Distribution of Fai' and Preventing Wealth Concentration
sectionsPreview.summary: Fai' is allocated to the Messenger, kinsmen, orphans, needy, and poor Muhajirun so wealth does not hoard.

sectionsPreview.title: Selflessness of Ansar and Hypocrites' False Promises
sectionsPreview.summary: The Ansar who prefer emigrants over themselves are praised, while the hypocrites' false promises to Banu Nadir fail.

sectionsPreview.title: Likeness of Banu Nadir and Satan's Betrayal
sectionsPreview.summary: Banu Nadir's fate mirrors recent predecessors, and hypocrites resemble Satan who incites disbelief and then disowns man.

sectionsPreview.title: Preparing for Tomorrow Through Taqwa and Remembrance
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are commanded to fear Allah, examine what they send ahead for tomorrow, and never forget Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Awe of the Qur'an Upon a Mountain
sectionsPreview.summary: Had the Qur'an descended upon a mountain it would have crumbled from fear of Allah, Knower of unseen.

sectionsPreview.title: The Most Beautiful Names and Majestic Attributes
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah Al-Hashr concludes with a magnificent proclamation of Allah's sovereign, holy, and creative attributes glorified by creation.

surahs.thematicSummary: Principles of foreign relations and alliances, examining migrating believing women, and the exemplary detachment of Prophet Ibrahim.

sectionsPreview.title: Prohibition of Secret Friendship with Hostile Enemies
sectionsPreview.summary: Revealed concerning Hatib's letter, these verses forbid believers from extending secret affection to hostile disbelievers.

sectionsPreview.title: Exemplary Disavowal of Idolatry by Prophet Ibrahim
sectionsPreview.summary: Blood ties will not avail on Judgment Day, and Prophet Ibrahim offers a noble example in disowning idolatry.

sectionsPreview.title: Future Reconciliation and Justice Toward Peaceful Non-Muslims
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah may replace enmity with affection, and He permits kindness and justice toward peaceful non-Muslims.

sectionsPreview.title: Allying with Aggressors and Examining Emigrant Women
sectionsPreview.summary: Alliance is forbidden with active aggressors, and emigrating believing women must be tested and kept from disbelievers.

sectionsPreview.title: Dower Compensation and Women's Pledge of Allegiance
sectionsPreview.summary: Rules govern compensating lost dowers and accepting the formal pledge of believing women to shun shirk and sin.

surahs.thematicSummary: Rebuking discrepancies between profession and practice, unified alignment in righteousness, and the supreme trade: faith and striving for forgiveness and triumph.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Glorification of the All-Mighty and All-Wise
sectionsPreview.summary: Surah As-Saff opens by declaring that everything in the heavens and earth proclaims the purity of Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Severe Odium of Saying What One Neglects
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are sternly admonished against making claims or promises that they fail to fulfill in action.

sectionsPreview.title: Fighting in Solid Rows and Prophetic Glad Tidings
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah loves those fighting in solid ranks, recalls Musa and 'Isa's tidings of Ahmad, and guarantees Islam's triumph.

sectionsPreview.title: The Profitable Trade of Faith and Striving
sectionsPreview.summary: The trade saving from painful punishment is believing in Allah and striving with wealth and life for Paradise.

sectionsPreview.title: Glad Tidings of Help and Near Victory
sectionsPreview.summary: Alongside eternal salvation, Allah promises believers a beloved worldly blessing of divine help and an imminent victory.

sectionsPreview.title: Becoming Helpers of Allah Like 'Isa's Disciples
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are called to be helpers of Allah's religion just as the disciples supported 'Isa and triumphed.

surahs.thematicSummary: The prophetic mission among the unlettered, the parable of carrying scripture without understanding, and the imperative duty of the Friday congregational prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Raising a Messenger Among the Unlettered Arabs
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah raised a Messenger among the unlettered to recite His verses, purify them, and teach the Book.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Mission and Parable of Unpracticed Scripture
sectionsPreview.summary: The Prophet's mission extends to future generations, while those ignoring the Torah resemble a donkey carrying books.

sectionsPreview.title: Challenging False Claims of Exclusive Divine Friendship
sectionsPreview.summary: Those claiming to be Allah's exclusive friends are challenged to wish for death, which they never do.

sectionsPreview.title: Inevitable Death and Hastening to Friday Prayer
sectionsPreview.summary: Death inevitably overtakes everyone, and believers must leave trade and hasten to remembrance when Friday prayer is called.

sectionsPreview.title: Seeking Livelihood After Jumu'ah and Prioritizing Worship
sectionsPreview.summary: After Friday prayer concludes, believers may seek Allah's bounty, remembering that Allah's reward excels trade and amusement.

surahs.thematicSummary: Unmasking the oaths of hypocrites, the psychological barrier of arrogance, and warnings against allowing wealth and children to distract from Allah's remembrance.

sectionsPreview.title: False Oaths and Cowardice of the Hypocrites
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah exposes the hypocrites as liars who use oaths as a shield, resemble timber, and fear every shout.

sectionsPreview.title: Arrogant Refusal to Seek Prophetic Forgiveness
sectionsPreview.summary: When invited to have the Messenger pray for their forgiveness, the hypocrites arrogantly turn their heads away.

sectionsPreview.title: Hypocrites' Economic Boycott Plot Against the Companions
sectionsPreview.summary: Hypocrites urge withholding charity so the Companions disperse, forgetting that heaven and earth's treasures belong to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Boast of Expulsion Refuted by True Honor
sectionsPreview.summary: Against the hypocrites' threat of expulsion, Allah declares that all honor belongs to Him, His Messenger, and believers.

sectionsPreview.title: Guarding Against Distraction by Wealth and Children
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are warned never to allow their possessions or children to distract them from remembering Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Spending in Charity Before the Arrival of Death
sectionsPreview.summary: Believers are urged to give charity before death arrives and a dying person begs in vain for respite.

surahs.thematicSummary: Universal glorification of God, the Day of Mutual Disillusion where true gain and loss are revealed, and cultivating family harmony through forbearance and charity.

sectionsPreview.title: Universal Praise and Humanity's Choice of Faith
sectionsPreview.summary: All creation glorifies Allah, the Sovereign Creator who formed humanity, among whom some disbelieve and some believe.

sectionsPreview.title: Perfection of Human Form and Certain Resurrection
sectionsPreview.summary: Allah shaped humans in the best form, reminds deniers of past ruins, and affirms that resurrection is certain.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Light and the Day of Gathering
sectionsPreview.summary: Humanity is called to believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the Qur'anic light before the Day of Gathering.

sectionsPreview.title: Patience in Calamities and Pardoning Family Trials
sectionsPreview.summary: Every calamity occurs by Allah's leave, guiding the believer's heart, and believers should pardon hindering family members.

sectionsPreview.title: Trial of Wealth and Guarding Against Greed
sectionsPreview.summary: Wealth and children are a test, so believers must practice Taqwa, overcome greed, and lend generously to Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: Juristic guidelines for divorce, calculating the waiting period ('iddah), equitable maintenance, and the famous promise of ease following hardship for those of Taqwa.

sectionsPreview.title: Regulations of Divorce and Waiting Period
sectionsPreview.summary: Establishes the proper timing for divorce, residence rights during the waiting period, and witnessing marital reconciliation or separation.

sectionsPreview.title: Reliance on Allah and Special Waiting Periods
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises divine provision for those who trust Allah and defines waiting periods for non-menstruating and pregnant women.

sectionsPreview.title: Housing, Maintenance, and Nursing Compensation for Divorcees
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands providing fair housing and financial support to divorced and pregnant women, alongside mutual consultation regarding nursing fees.

sectionsPreview.title: Proportional Maintenance and Fate of Rebellious Towns
sectionsPreview.summary: Directs husbands to spend on maintenance according to their means and warns against rebelling against divine commands.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophetic Guidance and Divine Omnipotence Over Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Calls believers to heed the Messenger who leads from darkness into light and affirms divine omnipotence.

surahs.thematicSummary: Domestic sensitivities in the prophetic household, the duty to shield one's family from spiritual destruction, and contrasting archetypes of righteous and rebellious women.

sectionsPreview.title: Unlawful Self-Prohibition and Expiation of Oaths
sectionsPreview.summary: Counsels the Prophet against forbidding lawful things to please his wives and mentions the prescribed expiation for oaths.

sectionsPreview.title: The Disclosed Secret and Admonition to Repent
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the disclosure of the Prophet's confidential matter by his wives and urges their sincere repentance before Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Qualities of Righteous Wives and Shielding Families
sectionsPreview.summary: Highlights the virtues of devout believing women and commands believers to protect themselves and their families from Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Sincere Repentance and Disbelieving Wives of Prophets
sectionsPreview.summary: Exhorts believers to sincere repentance, commands striving against disbelievers, and cites the unfaithful wives of Nuh and Lut.

sectionsPreview.title: Exemplary Faith of Asiyah and Chaste Maryam
sectionsPreview.summary: Presents Pharaoh's believing wife and Maryam daughter of Imran as supreme models of faith, devotion, and chastity.

surahs.thematicSummary: The protector from the punishment of the grave; creation of life and death as a test of deeds, flawless celestial architecture, and sustenance.

sectionsPreview.title: Supreme Divine Sovereignty and Purpose of Life
sectionsPreview.summary: Glorifies Allah's dominion over the universe and explains that life and death were created to test deeds.

sectionsPreview.title: Flawless Cosmic Creation and Regret in Hellfire
sectionsPreview.summary: Invites reflection on the flawless seven heavens, contrasts this with Hellfire, and affirms Allah knows all secrets.

sectionsPreview.title: The Subjugated Earth and Warning of Quakes
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds humanity of the serviceable earth while warning that Allah can cause it to swallow them.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Warnings and Sustaining Birds in Flight
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns disbelievers of stone-hurling winds like those that destroyed past nations and points to Allah holding birds aloft.

sectionsPreview.title: Helplessness and Delusion of the Stubborn Disbelievers
sectionsPreview.summary: Challenges disbelievers to find any helper or provider besides the All-Merciful if He withholds His sustenance.

sectionsPreview.title: Guided Walk Versus Blindness and Inevitable Reckoning
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the rightly guided believer with the blind straying person and answers the disbelievers' mockery regarding the Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Absolute Dependence on Allah for Flowing Water
sectionsPreview.summary: Asks who could restore flowing water to humanity if Allah were to cause their water to sink away.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oath by the Pen and written knowledge vindicating the Prophet's exalted moral character, the parable of the blighted orchard owners, and patience exemplified by Prophet Yunus.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Vindication of the Prophet's Exalted Character
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the pen to refute accusations of madness and affirms the Prophet's unceasing reward and noble character.

sectionsPreview.title: Steadfastness Against Compromises and Vile Slanderers
sectionsPreview.summary: Forbids yielding to the disbelievers' desire for compromise and condemns the arrogant, wealthy slanderer who mocks divine verses.

sectionsPreview.title: Humiliation of the Arrogant and Garden Owners
sectionsPreview.summary: Foretells the disgrace of the arrogant opponent and introduces the parable of the heedless garden owners.

sectionsPreview.title: Nighttime Destruction of the Miserly Brothers' Garden
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes how a divine calamity ruined the orchard overnight while its owners plotted to exclude the needy.

sectionsPreview.title: Shock and Realization at the Ruined Orchard
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the owners' shock upon discovering their devastated garden and their wisest brother's reminder to glorify Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Repentance and Remorse of the Garden Owners
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the brothers' confession of wrongdoing, mutual reproach, and hopeful repentance to their Lord for a better replacement.

sectionsPreview.title: Refuting Pagan Claims of Equal Afterlife Status
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebuts the disbelievers' claim of equal status in the Hereafter and warns of the Day of prostration.

sectionsPreview.title: Exhortation to Patience and Universal Quranic Reminder
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs the Prophet to remain patient unlike Yunus and affirms the Quran as a universal reminder.

surahs.thematicSummary: The undeniable reality of the resurrection, historical destruction of ancient deniers, the presenting of the cosmic record into the right or left hand, and confirmation of Quranic integrity.

sectionsPreview.title: The Inevitable Reality and Destruction of Deniers
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares the certainty of Judgment Day and recalls the devastating destruction of Thamud and 'Ad for denial.

sectionsPreview.title: Past Punishments, Nuh's Ark, and Cosmic Upheaval
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the gale destroying 'Ad, Pharaoh's ruin, Nuh's Ark, and the Trumpet blast shattering the cosmos.

sectionsPreview.title: Angels Bearing the Throne and Exposed Secrets
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes eight angels carrying the Divine Throne on Judgment Day when humanity is presented with no secret concealed.

sectionsPreview.title: Contrasting Joy and Despair at the Reckoning
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the joyful believer receiving his record in his right hand with the despairing left-handed sinner.

sectionsPreview.title: Shackling the Disbeliever Who Neglected the Needy
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts chaining and casting the culprit into Hellfire for disbelieving in Allah and neglecting the poor.

sectionsPreview.title: Bitter Torment and Divine Origin of Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the friendless sinner's foul food in Hell and swears that the Quran is divine revelation, not poetry.

sectionsPreview.title: Infallibility of Revelation and Certainty of Truth
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that any fabrication against Allah would be punished, proving the Quran is absolute divine truth.

surahs.thematicSummary: The ascending ways to the Divine, the nature of a Day spanning fifty thousand years, the human psychological cycle of fretfulness and stinginess, and the virtues of the steadfast in prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Mocking Demand for Torment and Graceful Patience
sectionsPreview.summary: Addresses a mocker's demand for immediate punishment from Allah and counsels the Prophet to graceful patience.

sectionsPreview.title: Horrors of Judgment and Desperate Ransom Wishes
sectionsPreview.summary: Portrays the terrifying Day when skies melt and sinners wish to ransom themselves with their families.

sectionsPreview.title: The Blazing Fire Calling Hoarders of Wealth
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the scorching flames of Hell that summon those who turned away from truth and hoarded wealth.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Impatience Cured by Steadfast Prayer
sectionsPreview.summary: Notes humanity's innate anxiety in hardship and stinginess in prosperity, excepting those who remain steadfast in regular prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Charity, Fear of Judgment, and Guarding Chastity
sectionsPreview.summary: Lists the virtues of the righteous who share wealth with the needy, fear punishment, and guard chastity.

sectionsPreview.title: Honoring Trusts and Humiliation of Arrogant Mockers
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises those who uphold trusts, testimonies, and prayers while warning mocking disbelievers of their humiliating resurrection.

surahs.thematicSummary: Noah's tireless multi-century summons to monotheism by night and day, seeking forgiveness for bountiful rain and prosperity, and his concluding prayer for all believing men and women.

sectionsPreview.title: Prophet Nuh's Mission and Call to Worship
sectionsPreview.summary: Introduces Allah's commission of Prophet Nuh to warn his people and summon them to worship and obey Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Nuh's Tireless Preaching and Promise of Forgiveness
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Nuh's lifelong public and private appeal to his arrogant people to seek forgiveness and receive abundant blessings.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Signs of Allah and Pagan Defiance
sectionsPreview.summary: Points to the seven heavens, sun, moon, and human creation from earth while Nuh laments his people's disobedience.

sectionsPreview.title: Stubborn Devotion to Five Ancient Idols
sectionsPreview.summary: Records the pagan leaders' insistence on worshipping Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr, leading many people astray.

sectionsPreview.title: Drowning of Wrongdoers and Nuh's Final Supplication
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the drowning of sinful disbelievers and Nuh's prayer for destroying tyrants and forgiving all believers.

surahs.thematicSummary: The jinn's awe upon hearing the wondrous recitation of the Quran, their renunciation of polytheism, and the affirmation that places of worship belong exclusively to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: The Jinn Listening and Believing in Quran
sectionsPreview.summary: Relates how a company of jinn heard the Quran, embraced its guidance, and affirmed Allah's absolute oneness.

sectionsPreview.title: Renouncing Pagan Delusions and Seeking Jinn Refuge
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts the jinn condemning lies against Allah and exposing how humans increased jinn arrogance by seeking refuge.

sectionsPreview.title: Guarded Heavens and Diverse Factions Among Jinn
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains how the heavens were barred with fiery meteors and notes righteous and deviant factions among jinn.

sectionsPreview.title: Rewards of Faith and Pure Worship in Mosques
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the fate of believing and deviant jinn and commands dedicating mosques and worship exclusively to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Timing of Judgment Known Only to Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs the Prophet to declare that only Allah knows the unseen and the appointed time of promised punishment.

sectionsPreview.title: Angelic Protection of Revelation Sent to Messengers
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that Allah reveals unseen matters to chosen messengers surrounded by angelic guards who preserve the divine message.

surahs.thematicSummary: Command to stand in contemplative night prayer (Tahajjud), reciting the Quran in slow measured tones (Tartil) to bear the weight of divine revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Command to Stand in Nightly Vigil Prayer
sectionsPreview.summary: Addresses the enwrapped Prophet with the command to spend a significant portion of the night in voluntary prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Measured Quranic Recitation and Weighty Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands reciting the Quran in a distinct, measured tone in preparation for receiving a weighty divine revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Spiritual Efficacy of Night Prayer Over Day
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that rising at night for worship best subdues the self and focuses speech amidst daytime engagements.

sectionsPreview.title: Exclusive Devotion and Reliance on the Lord
sectionsPreview.summary: Enjoins constant remembrance of Allah's name, complete spiritual devotion to Him, and taking Him alone as Guardian.

sectionsPreview.title: Patient Endurance and Gracious Parting From Deniers
sectionsPreview.summary: Counsels patience over the opponents' remarks, gracious avoidance of their hostility, and leaving affluent deniers to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Fetters, Blazing Fire, and Choking Food
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns the affluent deniers of the severe shackles, blazing fire, and choking food awaiting them with Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Easing of Night Vigil and Charitable Obligations
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns of Judgment Day with Pharaoh's example and grants concession in night prayer while enjoining charity and forgiveness.

surahs.thematicSummary: The inaugural command to arise and warn humanity, purify garments, shun pollution, and the solemn reckoning in the Fire of Saqar.

sectionsPreview.title: Call to Arise and Warn Humanity
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands the cloaked Prophet to rise from rest and begin publicly warning people against divine punishment.

sectionsPreview.title: Proclaiming Divine Greatness and Purifying Garments
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs the Prophet to magnify his Lord alone and maintain outward and inward purity of his garments.

sectionsPreview.title: Shunning Impurity and Selfless Generosity
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands abandoning all forms of idolatry and impurity and forbids giving favors to seek greater worldly returns.

sectionsPreview.title: Condemnation of Walid's Arrogance and Scorching Saqar
sectionsPreview.summary: Enjoins patience, warns of the Trumpet blast, and condemns the arrogant plotted slander against the Quran with Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Wisdom Behind Nineteen Angels Guarding Hellfire
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that the number of angelic wardens over Hell is a trial for disbelievers and strengthens believers' certainty.

sectionsPreview.title: Confessions of the Guilty in Scorching Saqar
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes how every soul is pledged for its deeds while sinners confess neglecting prayer, charity, and Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Fleeing From Reminder and Divine Will in Guidance
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebukes disbelievers who flee from the Quran like startled donkeys because they do not fear the Hereafter.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oaths by the Day of Resurrection and the self-reproaching conscience (An-Nafs al-Lawwamah), reconstructing human fingertips, and the radiant faces gazing upon their Lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Resurrection and Self-Reproaching Conscience
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by Resurrection Day and the self-reproaching soul to refute human doubts about Allah reassembling decayed bones.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Power to Restore Even Fingertips
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms Allah's power to reconstruct the finest details of human fingertips while exposing man's desire to sin.

sectionsPreview.title: Cosmic Eclipse and No Escape on Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Portrays the dazzling of sight and joining of sun and moon when man finds no refuge from reckoning.

sectionsPreview.title: Self-Testimony and Divine Preservation of Quranic Recitation
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares man a witness against himself and assures the Prophet that Allah will preserve and explain the Quran.

sectionsPreview.title: Radiant Faces, Deathbed Agony, and Arrogant Denial
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts believers beholding their Lord with gloomy deniers facing the inescapable throes of death after rejecting prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Embryonic Origin Proving Resurrection Power
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns the arrogant denier and proves Allah's power to resurrect the dead by recalling human creation from fluid.

surahs.thematicSummary: The origin of humanity from an intertwined drop, feeding the destitute, orphan, and captive solely for the sake of Allah, and the immortal gardens of camphor and ginger.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Creation for Testing and Camphor Drink
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalls man's creation from a mixed drop to test his gratitude and contrasts Hell's chains with Paradise's drink.

sectionsPreview.title: Gushing Springs for Servants Who Fulfill Vows
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the abundant heavenly spring enjoyed by righteous servants who fulfill their vows and fear Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Selfless Feeding of Needy and Paradisiacal Luxury
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises believers who feed the poor, orphans, and captives solely for Allah's sake and details their heavenly rewards.

sectionsPreview.title: Drinks of Salsabil, Silk Robes, and Silver
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the ginger-blended drink of Salsabil, immortal youths serving, and garments of fine silk and silver bracelets.

sectionsPreview.title: Gradual Revelation, Patient Worship, and Divine Will
sectionsPreview.summary: Urges the Prophet to patient perseverance and night worship while reminding humanity that guidance aligns with Allah's will.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oaths by the emissary winds of divine judgment, cosmic dissolution on the Day of Decision, punctuated ten times by: 'Woe on that Day to the deniers!'

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Winds and Angels Bringing Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by successive winds and angels delivering revelation that distinguishes truth from falsehood and removes all excuses.

sectionsPreview.title: Certainty of Judgment and Cosmic Dissolution
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares the promised Judgment inevitable when stars are extinguished, skies split, mountains scatter, and messengers are gathered.

sectionsPreview.title: Woe to Deniers and Destruction of Ancients
sectionsPreview.summary: Pronounces woe upon those who reject the truth and reminds them of the destruction of earlier sinful generations.

sectionsPreview.title: Signs in Human Creation and Three-Branched Shade
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts Allah's creation of humans and the earth's provisions before commanding deniers toward Hell's three-branched smoke.

sectionsPreview.title: Silenced Deniers Contrasted With Rewarded Righteous
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the silenced deniers facing castle-sized sparks on Judgment Day with the God-fearing enjoying shade, springs, and fruits.

sectionsPreview.title: Brief Worldly Enjoyment and Refusal to Bow
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns the guilty of their fleeting worldly enjoyment and condemns their stubborn refusal to bow in prayer.

sectionsPreview.title: Finality of the Quranic Discourse for Faith
sectionsPreview.summary: Challenges those who reject the clear Quran as to what other discourse they could possibly believe after it.

surahs.thematicSummary: The monumental inquiry regarding resurrection, cosmic stabilizers (mountains, sleep, celestial lamps), and the solemn Day when angels stand in ranks.

sectionsPreview.title: Disputing the Great Event Despite Terrestrial Signs
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebukes disbelievers questioning the Resurrection and points to the earth as a resting cradle and mountains as pegs.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Sleep, Night, Day, and Skies
sectionsPreview.summary: Enumerates divine signs in restful sleep, night's covering, daytime livelihood, seven firm heavens, and the blazing sun.

sectionsPreview.title: Rain-Fed Gardens and Trumpet of Decision Day
sectionsPreview.summary: Connects the revival of earth through rain to the appointed Day of Decision when the Trumpet is blown.

sectionsPreview.title: Hellfire Lying in Ambush for Transgressors
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns that Hellfire awaits rebellious transgressors for ages, offering no coolness or drink except boiling water and pus.

sectionsPreview.title: Fitting Recompense in Hell and Blissful Gardens
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that deniers receive fitting punishment for rejecting accountability while the God-fearing triumph with gardens and pure drinks.

sectionsPreview.title: Awe Before the Merciful and Regret of Disbelievers
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the solemn standing of angels on Truth Day when the disbeliever wishes he had remained mere dust.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oaths by the angels extracting souls, the downfall of Pharaoh's haughtiness, and the Great Overwhelming Event (At-Tammah al-Kubra).

sectionsPreview.title: Angels Extracting Disbelieving Souls With Force
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the angels who forcefully wrench out the souls of wicked disbelievers at the time of death.

sectionsPreview.title: Angels Gently Releasing the Souls of Believers
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the angels who smoothly and gently untie the souls of righteous believers upon their departure.

sectionsPreview.title: Angels Gliding Swiftly Through the Heavens
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the angels who float and glide swiftly through the cosmic realms in obedience to divine commands.

sectionsPreview.title: Angels Hastening Forward to Execute Commands
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the angels who race ahead rapidly to deliver souls and fulfill the decrees of their Lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Resurrection Quake and Pharaoh's Arrogant Claim
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms the two blasts of resurrection and recounts Musa confronting Pharaoh, who arrogantly claimed to be supreme lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Pharaoh's Exemplary Punishment and Cosmic Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalls Allah seizing Pharaoh as a warning, points to the creation of heaven and earth, and announces Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Hellfire Prepared for Rebels Preferring Worldly Life
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that whoever transgressed all bounds and preferred transient worldly life over the Hereafter will dwell in Hell.

sectionsPreview.title: Paradise for Self-Restraint and Suddenness of the Hour
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises Paradise to those who restrained desires out of awe of Allah, who alone knows the Hour.

surahs.thematicSummary: Divine admonition regarding the sincere blind seeker Ibn Umm Maktum, the universal value of humble truth-seeking, and the Deafening Blast of the Last Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Prioritizing the Sincere Blind Seeker Over Arrogant
sectionsPreview.summary: Gently reproves turning away from the blind seeker Ibn Umm Maktum while attending to indifferent pagan chiefs.

sectionsPreview.title: Exalted Scriptures and Condemnation of Human Ingratitude
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises the Quran's preservation in honored scrolls by noble angels and condemns man's stubborn ingratitude toward his Creator.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Creation and Proportioning From a Drop
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds arrogant man of his humble origin from a sperm-drop that Allah created and fashioned in due proportion.

sectionsPreview.title: Facilitating Life's Path, Death, and Resurrection
sectionsPreview.summary: Traces the human journey as Allah eases birth and guidance, decrees death and burial, and resurrects.

sectionsPreview.title: Reflecting on Earth's Nourishment Before the Blast
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebukes human failure to fulfill divine obligations and invites reflection on how rain and earth produce varied foods.

sectionsPreview.title: Fleeing From Kin and Contrasting Faces on Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the Day when people flee from closest relatives and faces divide into rejoicing believers and dust-stained disbelievers.

surahs.thematicSummary: The enfolding of the sun, falling of stars, boiling of oceans, accountability for the buried infant daughter, and the noble station of Archangel Jibril.

sectionsPreview.title: Folding of the Sun and Falling Stars
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the cosmic upheaval of the Last Day when the sun loses light, stars fall, and mountains move.

sectionsPreview.title: Abandoned Camels, Gathered Beasts, and Blazing Seas
sectionsPreview.summary: Portrays the terror when prized pregnant camels are neglected, wild beasts gather, and seas blaze with fire.

sectionsPreview.title: Pairing of Souls and Questioning Buried Infants
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes souls being grouped by deeds, the murdered infant girl being asked her crime, and scrolls laid open.

sectionsPreview.title: Unveiling of Recompense and Oaths by Celestial Signs
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the sky stripped away, Hell kindled, and Paradise brought near, followed by oaths by celestial signs.

sectionsPreview.title: Trustworthy Angelic Transmission and Universal Quranic Guidance
sectionsPreview.summary: Vindicates the Quran as conveyed by trustworthy Jibril and affirms that human guidance depends on Allah's will.

surahs.thematicSummary: The cleaving of heaven, scattering of stars, what deluded human beings concerning their Generous Lord, and the recording scribe angels.

sectionsPreview.title: Cleaving of the Sky and Overturning Graves
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the end of the world when the sky splits, stars scatter, seas burst forth, and graves overturn.

sectionsPreview.title: Every Soul Knowing Its Sent and Left Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that upon the cosmic upheaval, every soul will fully realize the deeds it sent ahead or neglected.

sectionsPreview.title: Rebuke of Human Deception Toward the Gracious Creator
sectionsPreview.summary: Questions what has deluded man into carelessness toward his Gracious Lord who created, perfected, and proportioned him.

sectionsPreview.title: Denial of Judgment and Noble Recording Angels
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds man of Allah's shaping of his form and warns that noble guardian angels record every human deed.

sectionsPreview.title: Contrasting Abodes of the Righteous and Sinners
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that the righteous will dwell in bliss while the wicked sinners will enter Hell on Judgment Day.

sectionsPreview.title: Inescapable Torment and Absolute Divine Sovereignty
sectionsPreview.summary: Emphasizes the gravity of Requital Day when sinners cannot escape Hell and all command belongs solely to Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: Condemnation of economic dishonesty and fraudulent weights, the ledger of the corrupt in Sijjin vs the ledger of the righteous in 'Illiyyun.

sectionsPreview.title: Condemnation of Commercial Fraud and Register of Sijjin
sectionsPreview.summary: Pronounces woe upon defrauders who demand full measure but give less, warning of resurrection and the Sijjin register.

sectionsPreview.title: Inscribed Record of Sinners and Rust on Hearts
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns sinful deniers of Judgment Day whose persistent evil deeds have coated their hearts with spiritual rust.

sectionsPreview.title: Veiling From Allah and Record in Illiyyun
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that disbelievers will be veiled from their Lord and burned, while the righteous record lies in 'Illiyyun.

sectionsPreview.title: Witnessed Register and Sealed Nectar of Tasnim
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the righteous reclining on thrones in radiant bliss, drinking pure musk-sealed nectar blended from the Tasnim spring.

sectionsPreview.title: Reversal of Mockery Between Believers and Guilty
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts how the wicked mocked believers in the world with how believers on thrones will witness their requital.

surahs.thematicSummary: The sky obeying its Lord in splitting, humanity's arduous labor progressing toward its Lord, and the receiving of records from right or behind the back.

sectionsPreview.title: Splitting of the Sky in Obedience to Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the sky splitting apart on the Last Day in rightful submission to the command of its Lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Stretching and Flattening of the Entire Earth
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the earth being stretched out flat and expanded to gather all creation on the Day of Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: The Earth Casting Out Its Buried Contents
sectionsPreview.summary: Portrays the earth disgorging all buried dead and treasures within it in complete obedience to its Lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Humanity's Inevitable Toil and Meeting With Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds every human being that life is a constant struggle leading inevitably to a direct meeting with Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Easy Reckoning Versus Receiving the Record Behind
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the joyful easy reckoning of the right-handed believer with the ruin of one given his book behind.

sectionsPreview.title: Worldly Heedlessness Under Allah's Constant Watch
sectionsPreview.summary: Explains that the doomed sinner lived heedlessly with family, assuming he would never return to his Lord.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Night Transitions and Human Stages
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by twilight, night, and the full moon that humanity will surely pass through successive existential stages.

sectionsPreview.title: Refusal to Prostrate and Unending Believers' Reward
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebukes disbelievers who refuse to prostrate upon hearing the Quran and contrasts their torment with believers' unending reward.

surahs.thematicSummary: The martyrdom of the People of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud) who perished for their faith, divine retribution against tyrants, and the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz).

sectionsPreview.title: Oath by the Sky and Stellar Constellations
sectionsPreview.summary: Opens with a solemn divine oath by the heaven adorned with mighty stellar formations and cosmic mansions.

sectionsPreview.title: Cursing the Tyrannical Makers of the Fiery Trench
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the Promised Day to condemn the cruel tyrants who burned believers alive solely for their faith.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Vengeance for Persecutors and Preserved Quran
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns unrepentant persecutors of Hellfire, recalls Pharaoh and Thamud's destruction, and exalts the Quran in the Preserved Tablet.

surahs.thematicSummary: The piercing star of the night, human biological origin from an emitted fluid, the Day when innermost secrets are laid bare, and the decisive nature of the Quran.

sectionsPreview.title: Oath by the Sky and Piercing Night-Star
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the heaven and the brightly piercing night-star to draw attention to divine watchfulness over creation.

sectionsPreview.title: Angelic Guardianship and Reflection on Human Origin
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that every soul has an appointed guardian angel and invites man to reflect on his origin.

sectionsPreview.title: Creation From Fluid Issuing Between Loins and Ribs
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds man that he was created from gushing fluid emerging from between the backbone and the chest-bones.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Power to Resurrect and Expose Secrets
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that the Creator can easily resurrect man on a Day when hidden secrets are tested without helper.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Returning Rain and Splitting Earth
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the sky that sends recurring rain and the earth that splits open with sprouting vegetation.

sectionsPreview.title: The Decisive Quranic Word and Foiling Plots
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms the Quran is a decisive word and assures the Prophet that Allah will foil pagan plots.

surahs.thematicSummary: Glorifying the Most High Lord who created and proportioned, divine ease in memorizing the Quran, purifying the soul, and continuity with the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa.

sectionsPreview.title: Glorifying the Name of the Most High Lord
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands believers to proclaim the transcendent purity of their Most High Lord's name above all defects.

sectionsPreview.title: Perfected Creation, Divine Measure, and Universal Guidance
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises Allah who created and proportioned all things and determined their precise measure and innate guidance.

sectionsPreview.title: Bringing Forth Green Pasturage and Dark Stubble
sectionsPreview.summary: Points to Allah's power in growing lush green pasture and subsequently reducing it to dark, dry stubble.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Guarantee of the Prophet's Quranic Memory
sectionsPreview.summary: Assures the Prophet that Allah will enable him to recite the revelation without forgetting except what Allah wills.

sectionsPreview.title: Facilitating the Path to the Easiest Way
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises to make easy for the Prophet the path of ease in following and conveying the Islamic law.

sectionsPreview.title: Beneficial Admonition Heeded by the God-Fearing
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands giving counsel, noting that the God-fearing accept it while the wretched avoid it and enter Hellfire.

sectionsPreview.title: Success Through Purification, Prayer, and Preferring Hereafter
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares true success for those who purify themselves and pray while rebuking preference for transient worldly life.

sectionsPreview.title: Teachings Confirmed in Scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that these foundational spiritual truths were likewise recorded in the earlier scriptures of Prophets Ibrahim and Musa.

surahs.thematicSummary: The overwhelming Last Day, contrasting downcast weary faces with radiant joyful souls in lofty gardens, and contemplation of camels, sky, mountains, and earth.

sectionsPreview.title: Announcement of the Overwhelming Day of Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Opens with an awakening question drawing attention to the solemn news of the Overwhelming Event of Resurrection.

sectionsPreview.title: Humbled and Exhausted Faces on Judgment Day
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the downcast, laboring, and exhausted faces of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment.

sectionsPreview.title: Scorching Fire and Drink From Boiling Springs
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the doomed entering a scorching fire and being given water to drink from a fiercely boiling spring.

sectionsPreview.title: Bitter Thorny Dari' as Food in Hellfire
sectionsPreview.summary: States that the inhabitants of Hell will have no food except a bitter, foul, and thorny plant.

sectionsPreview.title: Unnourishing Thorns Contrasted With Radiant Faces in Paradise
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts Hell's unnourishing food with the joyful, radiant faces of believers pleased with their striving in lofty gardens.

sectionsPreview.title: Peaceful Speech, Flowing Springs, and Raised Couches
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Paradise as free of vain talk and adorned with flowing springs and elevated couches of honor.

sectionsPreview.title: Placed Goblets, Arrayed Cushions, and Spread Carpets
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the refined luxuries of Paradise including ready goblets, lined cushions, and rich carpets spread out.

sectionsPreview.title: Reflections on Creation and Prophetic Duty of Reminder
sectionsPreview.summary: Invites reflection on camels, sky, mountains, and earth while reminding the Prophet that final reckoning belongs to Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oaths by the sacred dawn and ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah, historic destruction of Iram and Thamud, societal neglect of orphans and inheritance, and the Tranquil Soul (An-Nafs al-Mutma'innah).

sectionsPreview.title: Sacred Time Oaths and Fate of 'Ad
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by dawn, ten sacred nights, even and odd, and departing night before recalling the destruction of 'Ad.

sectionsPreview.title: Destruction of Iram, Thamud, and Tyrannical Pharaoh
sectionsPreview.summary: Recounts how Allah poured the scourge of punishment upon tall-pillared Iram, rock-carving Thamud, and stake-owning Pharaoh.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Watchfulness and Materialistic Neglect of Orphans
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms Allah's constant watch and critiques man's materialistic view of trials alongside his neglect of orphans and poor.

sectionsPreview.title: Devouring Inheritance, Greed, and Coming of Judgment
sectionsPreview.summary: Condemns devouring inheritance and excessive love of wealth before depicting the earth crushed and angels standing in rows.

sectionsPreview.title: Futile Regret at Hellfire and Contented Soul
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts the sinner's late regret when Hell is brought near with the welcoming call to the contented soul.

sectionsPreview.title: Invitation to Join Allah's Servants in Paradise
sectionsPreview.summary: Honors the tranquil believing soul with the divine invitation to join Allah's special servants and enter His Paradise.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oath by the sanctuary city of Makkah, humanity created in continuous struggle, and ascending the steep uphill road (Al-'Aqabah): freeing slaves and feeding hungry relatives in famine.

sectionsPreview.title: Solemn Divine Oath by the Sacred City
sectionsPreview.summary: Opens with an emphatic oath by the sacred city of Makkah to honor its sanctuary and prophetic resident.

sectionsPreview.title: The Prophet's Residence and Sanction in Makkah
sectionsPreview.summary: Honors the Prophet's presence in Makkah and foretells its lawful opening to him during the future conquest.

sectionsPreview.title: Oath by the Progenitor and Human Progeny
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the father of humanity, Adam, and all the offspring begotten through him across generations.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Life of Toil and Boastful Spending
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that man was created in struggle and rebukes his boastful arrogance in thinking no one sees him.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Sight, Speech, and Moral Choice
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds man of Allah's gifts of two eyes, a tongue, two lips, and guidance to distinguish both ways.

sectionsPreview.title: Scaling the Steep Path Through Selfless Charity
sectionsPreview.summary: Defines the steep moral ascent as freeing slaves and feeding kinsmen orphans and the destitute during famine.

sectionsPreview.title: Mutual Patience, Mercy, and Final Destinies
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises believers who enjoin patience and compassion as People of the Right Hand and warns disbelievers of Fire.

surahs.thematicSummary: Eleven consecutive oaths by cosmic phenomena and the proportioned human soul: true success lies in its spiritual purification (Tazkiyah) and failure in its corruption.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by the Sun and Following Moon
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the radiant sun and its brightness and by the moon as it follows in succession.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Revealing Day and Enveloping Night
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the daylight when it displays the sun's brilliance and the night when it covers the earth.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by the Sky and Spread Earth
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the heaven and the One who built it, and by the earth and its expansive spreading.

sectionsPreview.title: Proportioning the Soul and Inspiring Moral Discernment
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the human soul and how Allah proportioned it and inspired its awareness of wickedness and piety.

sectionsPreview.title: Purification of Soul Illustrated by Thamud's Ruin
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares success for purifying the soul and failure for corrupting it, exemplified by Thamud slaughtering Salih's she-camel.

surahs.thematicSummary: Contrasting human pursuits: the one who gives, fears God, and verifies righteousness is eased toward bliss; while the miserly skeptic is eased toward ruin.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Night, Day, and Gender Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the covering night, radiant day, and Creator of male and female to introduce human striving.

sectionsPreview.title: Divergent Human Striving, Charity, and God-Fearing Faith
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms that human efforts vary greatly, praising the one who gives in charity, fears Allah, and affirms truth.

sectionsPreview.title: Facilitating Ease for Generous and Hardship for Misers
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises ease toward Paradise for the generous believer and paves the path to distress for the arrogant miser.

sectionsPreview.title: Futile Wealth, Divine Guidance, and Warning of Fire
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that hoarded wealth cannot save a falling sinner, affirms Allah's sovereignty, and warns of a blazing Fire.

sectionsPreview.title: The Wretched Denier Entering the Blazing Fire
sectionsPreview.summary: States that none will burn in the blazing Fire except the most wretched who denied and turned away.

sectionsPreview.title: Salvation of the God-Fearing Who Spend for Purification
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises deliverance from Hellfire for the most God-fearing believer who gives his wealth in charity to purify himself.

sectionsPreview.title: Pure Sincerity Seeking the Countenance of Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Praises selfless charity given not to repay any worldly favor but solely to seek the pleasure of Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: Divine solace comforting the Prophet after an intermission in revelation: your Lord has neither forsaken nor hated you; the hereafter is better than the beginning; shelter the orphan and proclaim divine bounty.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Consolation and Promise of a Better Hereafter
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by morning light and night that Allah has not forsaken the Prophet and promises a better Hereafter.

sectionsPreview.title: Abundant Future Gifts and Shelter in Orphanhood
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises that Allah will grant the Prophet until he is well-pleased and recalls sheltering him as an orphan.

sectionsPreview.title: Blessings of Divine Guidance and Spiritual Enrichment
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds the Prophet how Allah guided him to sacred law and enriched him out of poverty.

sectionsPreview.title: Compassion Toward Orphans and Kindness to Petitioners
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands expressing gratitude for past blessings by never oppressing the orphan and never scolding the needy petitioner.

sectionsPreview.title: Proclaiming the Bounties of Your Gracious Lord
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs the Prophet and believers to openly proclaim and recount the favors and bounties of their Lord.

surahs.thematicSummary: The miraculous expansion of the Prophet's breast, lifting the burdensome weight from his back, elevating his remembrance, and the divine promise: with hardship comes ease.

sectionsPreview.title: Expansion of the Prophet's Bosom With Light
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds the Prophet of the immense favor of opening and illuminating his heart with wisdom and tranquility.

sectionsPreview.title: Relieving the Heavy Burden From the Prophet
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalls how Allah removed from the Prophet the heavy burden of anxiety that had weighed upon his back.

sectionsPreview.title: Exaltation of the Prophet's Renown and Mention
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares how Allah elevated the Prophet's name so it is honored alongside Allah's name throughout the world.

sectionsPreview.title: Double Assurance That Ease Accompanies Every Hardship
sectionsPreview.summary: Emphatically repeats the comforting divine promise that with every single hardship comes abundant ease and relief.

sectionsPreview.title: Devoted Worship After Completing Worldly Duties
sectionsPreview.summary: Instructs the Prophet to strive in worship upon completing public duties and turn eagerly toward his Lord.

surahs.thematicSummary: Oaths by the Fig, Olive, Mount Sinai, and the secure city of Makkah: humankind created in the finest aesthetic and moral proportion (Ahsani Taqweem), preserved only by faith and righteous deeds.

sectionsPreview.title: Oaths by Sacred Lands of Prophetic Revelation
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai, and the peaceful city of Makkah as sites of revelation.

sectionsPreview.title: Creation of Humanity in the Best Mold
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares as the subject of the oaths that Allah created humanity in the finest physical and spiritual form.

sectionsPreview.title: Return of the Ungrateful to Lowest Depths
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns that human beings who squander their noble potential are reduced to the lowest of the low.

sectionsPreview.title: Unending Reward for Believers Doing Righteous Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Exempts from degradation those who believe and perform righteous deeds, promising them an uninterrupted, eternal reward.

sectionsPreview.title: Inexcusability of Denying Judgment Before the Greatest Judge
sectionsPreview.summary: Questions what could cause anyone to deny the Final Judgment and affirms Allah as the Greatest of judges.

surahs.thematicSummary: The very first verses revealed at Cave Hira: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created', education by the Pen, warning against human insolence, and prostrating to draw near to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: First Revelation Commanding Recitation and Human Creation
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands reciting in the name of the Creator who fashioned the human being from a clinging clot.

sectionsPreview.title: Divine Generosity in Teaching Knowledge by the Pen
sectionsPreview.summary: Celebrates Allah as the Most Gracious who taught humanity knowledge by the pen that they did not know.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Transgression From Perceived Self-Sufficiency and Return
sectionsPreview.summary: Observes that man rebels when he deems himself self-sufficient, while reminding him of the inevitable return to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Rebuke of Abu Jahl Forbidding the Prophet's Prayer
sectionsPreview.summary: Condemns the arrogant tyrant who forbids Allah's servant from praying and warns of seizing his lying forelock.

sectionsPreview.title: Defying the Oppressor and Drawing Near Through Prostration
sectionsPreview.summary: Commands the Prophet never to obey the obstructor, but to prostrate and draw closer to Allah.

surahs.thematicSummary: The monumental descent of the Quran on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), a night of peace and angelic descent more virtuous than a thousand months.

sectionsPreview.title: Quranic Revelation in the Night Excelling Thousand Months
sectionsPreview.summary: Announces the revelation of the Quran in the Night of Decree, which surpasses a thousand months in virtue.

sectionsPreview.title: Descent of Angels and Jibril With Divine Decrees
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the angels and Jibril descending during that blessed night by their Lord's permission with every decreed matter.

sectionsPreview.title: All-Encompassing Peace Until the Rising of Dawn
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that the Night of Decree is pure peace and blessing lasting until the break of dawn.

surahs.thematicSummary: The clear evidence brought by the Prophet reciting purified scriptures, the core imperative of sincere monotheistic worship and prayer, and the best of all creation (Khayr al-Bariyyah).

sectionsPreview.title: Disbelievers Awaiting the Arrival of Clear Proof
sectionsPreview.summary: States that disbelievers among the People of the Book and polytheists would not desist until clear proof arrived.

sectionsPreview.title: The Messenger Reciting Purified and Upright Scriptures
sectionsPreview.summary: Identifies the clear proof as a Messenger from Allah reciting purified pages containing upright and lasting decrees.

sectionsPreview.title: Division of Scripture Peoples After Clear Proof Arrived
sectionsPreview.summary: Notes that the People of the Book split in stubborn disagreement only after the promised Prophet arrived.

sectionsPreview.title: Sincere Monotheism, Establishing Prayer, and Paying Zakah
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms they were commanded only to worship Allah with pure devotion, establish prayer, and give obligatory charity.

sectionsPreview.title: Contrasting the Worst and Best of Creatures
sectionsPreview.summary: Contrasts persistent disbelievers in Hell as the worst of creatures with righteous believers as the best of creatures.

sectionsPreview.title: Eternal Gardens and Mutual Pleasure for the God-Fearing
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises eternal gardens and mutual divine pleasure as the ultimate reward for those who fear their Lord.

surahs.thematicSummary: The cataclysmic final earthquake of the earth, yielding its burdens, and the exacting scrutiny where an atom's weight of good or evil will be seen.

sectionsPreview.title: The Earth Shaken by Its Final Convulsion
sectionsPreview.summary: Depicts the onset of the Last Day when the entire earth is violently shaken by its destined earthquake.

sectionsPreview.title: Earth's Testimony and Humanity Returning to See Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes the earth casting out its burdens, testifying by Allah's command, and people returning to see their deeds.

sectionsPreview.title: Seeing Every Atom's Weight of Good Performed
sectionsPreview.summary: Promises that whoever performs even an atom's weight of righteous good in the world will behold its reward.

sectionsPreview.title: Seeing Every Atom's Weight of Unrepented Evil
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns that whoever commits even an atom's weight of evil will likewise confront its consequence on Judgment Day.

surahs.thematicSummary: Dramatic oath by galloping steed charging at dawn and striking sparks of fire, exposing human ingratitude and passionate love for wealth, followed by the resurrection of the graves.

sectionsPreview.title: Oath by Panting War Horses Charging Forth
sectionsPreview.summary: Opens with an oath by the swift steeds that run panting in the cause of Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Charging Steeds Witnessing Human Ingratitude Toward Allah
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by horses striking sparks and charging at dawn to declare that man is ungrateful to Allah.

sectionsPreview.title: Humanity's Intense and Passionate Love for Wealth
sectionsPreview.summary: Exposes how the ungrateful human being is fiercely consumed by an excessive love for worldly wealth.

sectionsPreview.title: Overturning of Graves and Exposure of Heart Secrets
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns heedless man of the Day when graves are overturned, hearts' secrets are laid bare, and Allah judges.

surahs.thematicSummary: The terrifying Striking Calamity when people will be like scattered moths and mountains like carded wool, weighing deeds upon the divine balance.

sectionsPreview.title: The Striking Calamity and Weighing of Human Deeds
sectionsPreview.summary: Portrays the catastrophic Day when people scatter like moths and destinies are decided by heavy or light scales.

surahs.thematicSummary: Severe condemnation of rivalry in worldly accumulation that diverts humanity until they visit the graves, and the ultimate interrogation concerning worldly pleasures.

sectionsPreview.title: Distraction by Mutual Rivalry in Worldly Gain
sectionsPreview.summary: Rebukes humanity for being diverted from Allah and the Hereafter by competitive boasting and amassing worldly goods.

sectionsPreview.title: Heedlessness Until Death and Repeated Warnings
sectionsPreview.summary: Warns that worldly rivalry persists until people enter their graves, followed by emphatic warnings of coming realization.

sectionsPreview.title: Awakening Through True Knowledge of Certainty
sectionsPreview.summary: Declares that if people possessed true knowledge of certainty regarding the Hereafter, worldly greed would never distract them.

sectionsPreview.title: Inevitable Sight of the Blazing Hellfire
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears emphatically that humanity will surely behold the blazing Fire of Hell in the Hereafter.

sectionsPreview.title: Eye of Certainty and Questioning About Worldly Blessings
sectionsPreview.summary: Affirms they will see Hell with the eye of certainty and be questioned about every worldly blessing enjoyed.

surahs.thematicSummary: A profound three-verse declaration: oath by the token of Time that all humanity is in loss, except those who believe, perform righteous deeds, and enjoin truth and patience.

sectionsPreview.title: Human Loss and the Four Pillars of Salvation
sectionsPreview.summary: Swears by time that humanity is in loss except believers who do good and enjoin truth and patience.

surahs.thematicSummary: Woe to every backbiter and slanderer who hoards wealth imagining it confers immortality, cast into the Crushing Fire (Al-Hutamah) vaulted upon lofty columns.

sectionsPreview.title: Woe to Every Slanderer and Backbiter
sectionsPreview.summary: Pronounces severe destruction and woe upon every habitual backbiter, slanderer, and derider of others.

sectionsPreview.title: Delusion of Hoarded Wealth and the Crushing Fire
sectionsPreview.summary: Condemns the greedy hoarder who thinks wealth makes him immortal and warns he will be cast into al-Hutamah.

sectionsPreview.title: Fire Piercing Hearts in Outstretched Columns
sectionsPreview.summary: Describes Allah's kindled Fire penetrating directly into hearts while vaulted over the condemned in outstretched columns.

surahs.thematicSummary: The miraculous defense of the Holy Ka'bah against the invading army of Abraha and his war elephants through flights of birds (Ababil) casting baked stones.

sectionsPreview.title: Foiling the Plot of the Army of Elephants
sectionsPreview.summary: Reminds the Quraysh how Allah foiled Abraha's elephant army when they marched to destroy the Sacred Ka'bah.

sectionsPreview.title: Swarms of Birds Sent Against the Invaders
sectionsPreview.summary: Recalls how Allah dispatched flocks of flying birds against the invading army to protect His Sacred House.

sectionsPreview.title: Pelting the Army With Stones of Baked Clay
